symbols.name: CONFIG_LLMNR_RESOLVER
symbols.help:
This option enables link local multicast name resolution client side
support. See RFC 4795 for details. LLMNR is typically used by Windows
hosts. If you enable this option, then the DNS requests are ONLY sent
to LLMNR well known multicast address 224.0.0.252:5355 or
[ff02::1:3]:5355 and other DNS server addresses are ignored.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > Network Protocols > DNS resolver

symbols.name: CONFIG_LLMNR_RESOLVER_ADDITIONAL_BUF_CTR
symbols.help: Number of additional buffers available for the LLMNR responder.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > Network Protocols > LLMNR responder

symbols.name: CONFIG_LLMNR_RESPONDER
symbols.help:
This option enables the LLMNR responder support for Zephyr.
It will listen well-known address ff02::1:3 and 224.0.0.252.
Currently this only returns IP address information.
You must set CONFIG_NET_HOSTNAME to some meaningful value and
then LLMNR will start to respond to <hostname> LLMNR queries.
Note that LLMNR queries should only contain single-label names
so there should be NO dot (".") in the name (RFC 4795 ch 3).
Current implementation does not support TCP.
See RFC 4795 for more details about LLMNR.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > Network Protocols

symbols.name: CONFIG_LLMNR_RESPONDER_INIT_PRIO
symbols.prompt: Startup priority for the LLMNR responder init
symbols.help:
Note that if NET_CONFIG_AUTO_INIT is enabled, then this value
should be bigger than its value.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > Network Protocols > LLMNR responder

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOAPIC_SPURIOUS_VECTOR
symbols.help:
A special situation may occur when a processor raises its task
priority to be greater than or equal to the level of the
interrupt for which the processor INTR signal is currently being
asserted. If at the time the INTA cycle is issued, the
interrupt that was to be dispensed has become masked (programmed
by software), the local APIC will deliver a spurious-interrupt
vector. Dispensing the spurious-interrupt vector does not affect
the ISR, so the handler for this vector should return without an EOI.
From x86 manual Volume 3 Section 10.9.

If this value is left at -1 the last entry in the IDT will be used.

[2001:db8::2]

supported by the given MCU. Not all debug probes support high

set to 0 it means log will not be activated for those modules.
Levels are:

- 0 OFF, do not write by default
- 1 ERROR, default to only write LOG_LEVEL_ERR
- 2 WARNING, default to write LOG_LEVEL_WRN
- 3 INFO, default to write LOG_LEVEL_INFO
- 4 DEBUG, default to write LOG_LEVEL_DBG

Dictionary based logging is binary based where predefined strings
are replaced with their equivalent addresses from the built binary
image file in log output. This reduces the size required to store
the log output when there are long format strings to be logged.

This should be selected by the backend automatically.

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_FRONTEND_STMESP_EARLY_BUF_SIZE
symbols.prompt: Buffer size to store early messages
symbols.help:
Frontend cannot write to STM if it is used with ETR buffer unless ETR is
initialized and memory is properly configured (privileges). Data is stored
in the buffer and flushed to the STMESP once the pipeline is ready.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Frontends > Coresight STM frontend

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_FRONTEND_STMESP_FLUSH_COUNT
symbols.help:
Before going to sleep CPU shall write to STM some dummy data to ensure
that any buffered data goes to TPIU/ETR.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Frontends > Coresight STM frontend

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_FRONTEND_STMESP_FSC
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Frontends > Coresight STM frontend

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_FRONTEND_STMESP_GUARANTEED_ACCESS
symbols.help:
When enabled, accessing STMESP registers will stall if write cannot be
performed (e.g. ETR buffer is full).
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Frontends > Coresight STM frontend

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_FRONTEND_STMESP_MSG_END_TIMESTAMP
symbols.prompt: Generate timestamp and marker at message end
symbols.help:
Generate a zero data byte with timestamp and marker at message end,
instead of generating a timestamp and marker at message start and
a flag at end. This can be used to maintain compatibility with
certain decoders.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Frontends > Coresight STM frontend

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_FRONTEND_STMESP_TP_CHAN_BASE
symbols.help: Do not change this value as it is aligned with host decoder (nrfutil trace).
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Frontends

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_FRONTEND_STMESP_TURBO_DROP_OTHERS
symbols.prompt: Drop all logs except turbo logs
symbols.help:
Option can be enabled for memory constraint cases to remove all logging
related code except turbo logs.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Frontends > Coresight STM frontend

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_FRONTEND_STMESP_TURBO_LOG
symbols.help:
When enabled, then logging messages with 0 and 1 numeric argument are
optimized and handled much faster than others.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Frontends > Coresight STM frontend

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_FUNC_NAME_PREFIX_DBG
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting > Prepend non-hexdump log message with function name

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_FUNC_NAME_PREFIX_ERR

symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting > Prepend non-hexdump log message with function name

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_FUNC_NAME_PREFIX_WRN
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting > Prepend non-hexdump log message with function name

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_IMMEDIATE_CLEAN_OUTPUT
symbols.help:
If enabled, interrupts are locked during whole log message processing.
As a result, processing on one log message cannot be interrupted by
another one and output is clean, not interleaved. However, enabling
this option is causing interrupts locking for significant amount of
time (up to multiple milliseconds).
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_INFO_COLOR_GREEN
symbols.prompt: Use green color for info level logs
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting > Colors in the backend

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_LINK_IPC_SERVICE
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_LINK_IPC_SERVICE_BUFFER_SIZE
symbols.help:
Dedicated buffer allows to maintain ordering of processed messages.
If 0, main buffer is used and messages are processed in the order of
arrival.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > IPC service link

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_MAX_LEVEL
symbols.prompt: Maximal log level compiled in the system
symbols.help:
Forces a maximal log level for all modules. Modules saturates their
specified level if it is greater than this option, otherwise they use
the level specified by this option instead of their default or
whatever was manually set.
Levels are:

- 0 OFF, logging is turned off
- 1 ERROR, maximal level set to LOG_LEVEL_ERR
- 2 WARNING, maximal level set to LOG_LEVEL_WRN
- 3 INFO, maximal level set to LOG_LEVEL_INFO
- 4 DEBUG, maximal level set to LOG_LEVEL_DBG
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Logging levels filtering

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_MEM_UTILIZATION
symbols.help:
When enabled, maximum usage of memory used for log messages in deferred
mode is tracked. It can be used to trim LOG_BUFFER_SIZE.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Misc

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_MIPI_SYST_ARGS_BUFFER_SIZE
symbols.help:
This user-configurable option specifies the maximum size (in bytes) to reserve in
the call stack for processing the logging format strings MIPI Sys-T library.
Increasing it will allow for longer strings to be logged at the expense of used
stack space. Conversely decreasing it will lessen the stack burden at the expense
of shorter maximum log strings.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting > MIPI SyS-T format output

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_MIPI_SYST_CATALOG_ARGS_BUFFER_SIZE
symbols.prompt: Size of temporary arguments buffer when using Sys-T Catalog
symbols.help:
The size (in bytes) of the temporary buffer to store the expanded
argument list needed for the MIPI Sys-T library for processing
catalog messages.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting > MIPI SyS-T format output

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_MIPI_SYST_DISABLE_TIMESTAMP
symbols.help: Remove the timestamp from the MIPI Sys-T protocol.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting > MIPI SyS-T format output

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_MIPI_SYST_ENABLE
symbols.help: Enable MIPI SyS-T format output for the logger system.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_MIPI_SYST_MSG_DEFAULT_MODULE_ID
symbols.prompt: Default module ID in Sys-T message
symbols.help:
The default module ID embedded in the origin unit in
Sys-T message header.

If CONFIG_LOG_MIPI_SYST_OUTPUT_LOG_MSG_SRC_ID is disabled,
this will be used for all Sys-T messages.

If CONFIG_LOG_MIPI_SYST_OUTPUT_LOG_MSG_SRC_ID is enabled,
this will be used for log messages without source IDs,
for example, printk() if CONFIG_LOG_PRINTK is enabled.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting > MIPI SyS-T format output

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_MIPI_SYST_MSG_DEFAULT_UNIT_ID
symbols.prompt: Default unit ID in Sys-T message
symbols.help:
The default unit ID embedded in the origin unit in
Sys-T message header.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting > MIPI SyS-T format output

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_MIPI_SYST_OUTPUT_LOG_MSG_SRC_ID
symbols.prompt: Output Log Message Source ID as Module ID
symbols.help:
Enable this option to output the log message source ID
as the Sys-T message module ID (as in origin unit in Sys-T
message header).
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting > MIPI SyS-T format output

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_MIPI_SYST_USE_CATALOG
symbols.prompt: Use MIPI Sys-T Catalog for logging
symbols.help: Use MIPI Sys-T Catalog for logging instead of plain text.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting > MIPI SyS-T format output

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_MODE
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_MODE_DEFERRED
symbols.help:
Log messages are buffered and processed later. This mode has the
least impact on the application. Time consuming processing is
deferred to the known context.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Mode

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_MODE_IMMEDIATE
symbols.help:
When enabled log is processed in the context of the call. It impacts
performance of the system since time consuming operations are
performed in the context of the log entry (e.g. high priority
interrupt).Logger backends must support exclusive access to work
flawlessly in that mode because one log operation can be interrupted
by another one in the higher priority context.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Mode

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_MODE_MINIMAL
symbols.help:
Enable minimal logging implementation. This has very little footprint
overhead on top of the printk() implementation for standard
logging macros. Hexdump macros are also supported, with a small
amount of code pulled in if used. Build time filtering is supported,
but not runtime filtering. There are no timestamps, prefixes,
colors, or asynchronous logging, and all messages are simply
sent to printk().
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Mode

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_MODE_OVERFLOW
symbols.help:
If enabled, then if there is no space to log a new message, the
oldest one is dropped. If disabled, current message is dropped.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Processing

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_MSG_APPEND_RO_STRING_LOC
symbols.help:
Enable this option to force log messages to always append location of
read-only string arguments in the package. This should be selected by
backends if required.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Misc

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_MULTIDOMAIN
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_OUTPUT
symbols.help:
Module which provides formatting of log messages to a human-readable
strings.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_OUTPUT_FORMAT_CUSTOM_TIMESTAMP
symbols.help:
Enable support for custom formatter for the timestamp.
It will be applied to all backends except the syslog net backend.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting > Timestamp format mode

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_OUTPUT_FORMAT_DATE_TIMESTAMP
symbols.help: When enabled timestamp is formatted to YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss.ms,us.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting > Timestamp format mode

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_OUTPUT_FORMAT_ISO8601_TIMESTAMP
symbols.help: When enabled timestamp is formatted to YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss,ffffffZ.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting > Timestamp format mode

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_OUTPUT_FORMAT_LINUX_TIMESTAMP
symbols.help:
This formatting is something in the middle between the pure raw format
and the hh:mm:ss:ms,us one. It resembles the Linux's kernel format in
which timestamps are printed as fixed point values with seconds on the
left side of the point and microseconds on the right side.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting > Timestamp format mode

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_OUTPUT_FORMAT_TIME_TIMESTAMP
symbols.help: When enabled timestamp is formatted to hh:mm:ss.ms,us.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting > Timestamp format mode

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_OVERRIDE_LEVEL
symbols.help:
Forces a minimum log level for all modules. Modules use their
specified level if it is greater than this option, otherwise they use
the level specified by this option instead of their default or
whatever was manually set.
Levels are:

- 0 OFF, do not override
- 1 ERROR, override to write LOG_LEVEL_ERR
- 2 WARNING, override to write LOG_LEVEL_WRN
- 3 INFO, override to write LOG_LEVEL_INFO
- 4 DEBUG, override to write LOG_LEVEL_DBG
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Logging levels filtering

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_PRINTK
symbols.help:
If enabled, printk messages are redirected to the logging subsystem.
The messages are formatted in place and logged unconditionally.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Processing

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_PROCESSING_LATENCY_US
symbols.help:
Arbitrary time between log message creation in the remote domain and
processing in the local domain. Higher value increases message processing
latency but increases chances of maintaining correct ordering of the
messages. Option is used only if links are using dedicated buffers
for remote messages.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Processing > Use internal thread for log processing

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_PROCESS_THREAD
symbols.prompt: Use internal thread for log processing
symbols.help:
When enabled thread is created by the logger subsystem. Thread is
waken up periodically (see LOG_PROCESS_THREAD_SLEEP_MS) and whenever
number of buffered messages exceeds the threshold (see
LOG_PROCESS_TRIGGER_THR).
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Processing

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_PROCESS_THREAD_CUSTOM_PRIORITY
symbols.help: Set a custom value for the log processing thread.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Processing > Use internal thread for log processing

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_PROCESS_THREAD_PRIORITY
symbols.prompt: Priority of the log processing thread
symbols.help:
The priority of the log processing thread.
When not set the priority is set to K_LOWEST_APPLICATION_THREAD_PRIO.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Processing > Use internal thread for log processing > Custom log thread priority

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_PROCESS_THREAD_SLEEP_MS
symbols.prompt: Set internal log processing thread sleep period
symbols.help:
Log processing thread sleeps for requested period given in
milliseconds. When waken up, thread process any buffered messages.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Processing > Use internal thread for log processing

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_PROCESS_THREAD_STACK_SIZE
symbols.prompt: Stack size for the internal log processing thread
symbols.help: Set the internal stack size for log processing thread.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Processing > Use internal thread for log processing

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_PROCESS_THREAD_STARTUP_DELAY_MS
symbols.prompt: Set log processing thread startup delay
symbols.help:
Log processing thread starts after requested delay given in
milliseconds. When started, thread process any buffered messages.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Processing > Use internal thread for log processing

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_PROCESS_TRIGGER_THRESHOLD
symbols.prompt: Number of buffered log messages before flushing
symbols.help:
When number of buffered messages reaches the threshold thread is waken
up. Log processing thread ID is provided during log initialization.
Set 0 to disable the feature. If LOG_PROCESS_THREAD is enabled then
this threshold is used by the internal thread.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Processing

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_RATELIMIT
symbols.help:
When enabled, provides rate-limited logging macros that prevent
log flooding when messages are generated frequently. Rate limiting
is per-macro-call-site, meaning each unique call has its own
independent rate limit.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_RATELIMIT_FALLBACK
symbols.prompt: Fallback behavior for rate-limited logging macros
symbols.help:
Select fallback behavior for rate-limited logging macros when
LOG_RATELIMIT is disabled.

- "Log all prints": All log prints are output, i.e., rate limiting is ignored.
- "Drop all prints": All log prints using rate-limited macros are dropped.

This option allows you to control whether rate-limited log macros
should always print or be completely suppressed when rate limiting
is not available.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_RATELIMIT_FALLBACK_DROP
symbols.help: All log prints using rate-limited macros are dropped (no output).
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Fallback behavior for rate-limited logging macros

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_RATELIMIT_FALLBACK_LOG
symbols.help: All log prints using rate-limited macros are output as normal logs.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Fallback behavior for rate-limited logging macros

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_RATELIMIT_INTERVAL_MS
symbols.help:
Default interval between rate-limited log messages.
This is used by the convenience macros LOG_*_RATELIMIT
when no explicit rate is provided. Can be overridden per call
using LOG_*_RATELIMIT_RATE macros.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Rate-limited logging macros

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_REMOTE_DOMAIN_MAX_COUNT
symbols.help: Number of domains that can be handled by a link
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Misc

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_RUNTIME_DEFAULT_LEVEL
symbols.prompt: Default runtime log level at startup
symbols.help:
Sets the initial runtime filter level for all modules at system startup.
This level is applied before any backend or application-specific filtering
is configured. Useful for controlling logging verbosity at boot before
dynamic reconfiguration via IPC or other mechanisms.

Levels are:
- 0 OFF, no logs at startup
- 1 ERROR, only errors shown at startup
- 2 WARNING, errors and warnings at startup
- 3 INFO, info level and above at startup
- 4 DEBUG, all logs including debug at startup

Note: This affects runtime filtering only. Compile-time log levels
are controlled by CONFIG_LOG_MAX_LEVEL and per-module settings.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Logging levels filtering > Runtime filtering reconfiguration

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_RUNTIME_FILTERING
symbols.help:
Allow runtime configuration of maximal, independent severity
level for instance.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Logging levels filtering

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_SIMPLE_MSG_OPTIMIZE
symbols.help:
Dedicated code for handling simple log messages (0-2 32 bit word arguments).
Approximately, 70%-80% log messages in the application fit into that category.
Depending on the architecture code size reduction is from 0-40% (highest seen on
RISCV32) and execution time also up to 40%.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Misc

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_SOURCE_NAME_CACHE_ENTRY_COUNT
symbols.prompt: Number of entries in source name cache
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Processing

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_SOURCE_NAME_CACHE_ENTRY_SIZE
symbols.prompt: Cache slot size of source name
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Processing

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_SPEED
symbols.help: If enabled, logging may take more code size to get faster logging.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Processing

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_TAG_DEFAULT
symbols.help: Initial tag.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_TAG_MAX_LEN
symbols.help:
Setting non-zero value enables option to specify a tag which is
prepended to each log message. Tag can be changed at runtime.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_TEST_CLEAR_MESSAGE_SPACE
symbols.help:
Used in testing to simplify message comparison if message contains
paddings.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Misc

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_THREAD_ID_PREFIX
symbols.help:
Enable support for prefixing log message with thread name or ID.
Thread name is used if THREAD_NAME is enabled.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Output Formatting

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_TIMESTAMP_64BIT
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Processing

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_TIMESTAMP_USE_REALTIME
symbols.prompt: Use real time clock for timestamp
symbols.help: When enabled, real time clock is used for timestamping.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Processing

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_TRACE_SHORT_TIMESTAMP
symbols.help:
When enabled, shorter timestamp is used and trace message is
compressed.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Processing

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_USE_TAGGED_ARGUMENTS
symbols.help: If enabled, packaging uses tagged arguments.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Misc

symbols.name: CONFIG_LOG_USE_VLA
symbols.help:
Using VLA slightly decreases stack usage in some cases it may not be
supported. Note that VLA are used for arrays which size is resolved at
compile time so at runtime arrays have fixed size.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Logging > Logging > Misc

symbols.name: CONFIG_LORA
symbols.help: Include LoRa drivers in the system configuration.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Device Drivers

symbols.name: CONFIG_LORAWAN
symbols.help: This option enables LoRaWAN support.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services

symbols.name: CONFIG_LORAWAN_APP_CLOCK_SYNC
symbols.help:
Enables the LoRaWAN Application Layer Clock Synchronization service
according to LoRa Alliance TS003-2.0.0.

The service uses the default port 202.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > LoRaWAN support [EXPERIMENTAL] > LoRaWAN Services backend

symbols.name: CONFIG_LORAWAN_APP_CLOCK_SYNC_PERIODICITY
symbols.help:
Initial setting for clock synchronization periodicity in seconds.

The value can be updated remotely by the application server within a
range from 128 (0x80) to 4194304 (0x400000).

Default setting: 24h.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > LoRaWAN support [EXPERIMENTAL] > LoRaWAN Services backend > Application Layer Clock Synchronization

symbols.name: CONFIG_LORAWAN_EMUL
symbols.help:
The emulator can be used for unit testing of LoRaWAN services.
It provides interfaces to send arbitrary messages to the LoRaWAN
stack and receive the response through callbacks without using
actual LoRa hardware.

See include/zephyr/lorawan/emul.h for the emulator API.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > LoRaWAN support [EXPERIMENTAL]

symbols.name: CONFIG_LORAWAN_FRAG_TRANSPORT
symbols.help:
Enables the LoRaWAN Fragmented Data Block Transport service
according to TS004-1.0.0 as published by the LoRa Alliance.

The used default port for this service is 201.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > LoRaWAN support [EXPERIMENTAL] > LoRaWAN Services backend

symbols.name: CONFIG_LORAWAN_FRAG_TRANSPORT_DECODER
symbols.prompt: Fragmented Data Block Transport decoder implementation
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > LoRaWAN support [EXPERIMENTAL] > LoRaWAN Services backend > Fragmented Data Block Transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_LORAWAN_FRAG_TRANSPORT_DECODER_LOWMEM
symbols.help: Alternate implementation with reduced RAM footprint.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > LoRaWAN support [EXPERIMENTAL] > LoRaWAN Services backend > Fragmented Data Block Transport > Fragmented Data Block Transport decoder implementation

symbols.name: CONFIG_LORAWAN_FRAG_TRANSPORT_DECODER_SEMTECH
symbols.help: The default decoder implementation from LoRaMAC-node.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > LoRaWAN support [EXPERIMENTAL] > LoRaWAN Services backend > Fragmented Data Block Transport > Fragmented Data Block Transport decoder implementation

symbols.name: CONFIG_LORAWAN_FRAG_TRANSPORT_IMAGE_SIZE
symbols.help:
Size of the flash partition for the application firmware image
in bytes.

The minimum number of fragments to be transferred is calculated from
this value divided by the fragment size.

This setting has significant influence on RAM usage.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > LoRaWAN support [EXPERIMENTAL] > LoRaWAN Services backend > Fragmented Data Block Transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_LORAWAN_FRAG_TRANSPORT_MAX_FRAG_SIZE
symbols.help:
Maximum size of one fragment transferred during the fragmented data
block transport session of the FUOTA process. It is chosen on the
server side.

The fragment has to fit into the LoRaWAN payload, which can be up to
242 bytes depending on the region and frequency settings. 3 bytes of
the payload are consumed for protocol information.

For some MCUs like the STM32WL the fragment size has to be a multiple
of 8 (see flash driver for further information).

This setting has significant influence on RAM usage. If the exact
fragment size is known, use that value for MIN and MAX config to
reduce memory consumption.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > LoRaWAN support [EXPERIMENTAL] > LoRaWAN Services backend > Fragmented Data Block Transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_LORAWAN_FRAG_TRANSPORT_MAX_REDUNDANCY
symbols.help:
The built-in forward error correction (FEC) mechanism allows to
reconstruct missed packages from additional redundant packages
sent by the server after all packages have been sent.

This parameter specifies the maximum amount of packet loss (in
percent) for which it should be possible to reconstruct the full
firmware image.

This setting has significant influence on RAM usage.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > LoRaWAN support [EXPERIMENTAL] > LoRaWAN Services backend > Fragmented Data Block Transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_LV_DRAW_THREAD_PRIO
symbols.prompt: Thread priority for the drawing thread
symbols.help:
Thread priority controls the relative importance of the drawing threads.
Values correspond to lv_thread_prio_t enum in lv_os.h:
0: LV_THREAD_PRIO_LOWEST
1: LV_THREAD_PRIO_LOW
2: LV_THREAD_PRIO_MID (default)
3: LV_THREAD_PRIO_HIGH
4: LV_THREAD_PRIO_HIGHEST

Higher priority can improve rendering performance but might cause
starvation of lower priority tasks.

symbols.help:

configuration the entropy module is used to gather some data and then
either ctr_drbg or hmac_drbg are applied on top of it to improve
the randomness.

sources which are enabled in the system: if weak entropy sources are
used, then the generated data will only be pseudo random. Strong
entropy sources are strongly recommended (if possible) to have real

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_APPLICATION_FIRMWARE_UPDATER
symbols.help:
Select this if the current image is the firmware updater image. This will use slot 1
information when signing the image.

Note that the zephyr chosen node ``zephyr,code-partition`` should be set to
``slot1_partition`` for this image.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Modules > MCUboot bootloader support > On board MCUboot operation mode

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_MODE
symbols.prompt: Application assumed MCUboot mode of operation
symbols.help:
Informs application build on assumed MCUboot mode of operation.
This is important for validataing application against DT configuration,
which is done by west sign.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Modules > MCUboot bootloader support > On board MCUboot operation mode

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_MODE_DIRECT_XIP
symbols.prompt: MCUboot has been configured for DirectXIP operation
symbols.help:
MCUboot expects slot0_partition and slot1_partition to exist in DT.
In this mode MCUboot can boot from either partition and will
select one with higher application image version, which usually
means major.minor.patch triple, unless BOOT_VERSION_CMP_USE_BUILD_NUMBER
is also selected that enables comparison of build number.
This option automatically selects
MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_NO_DOWNGRADE as it is not possible
to swap back to older version of application.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Modules > MCUboot bootloader support > On board MCUboot operation mode > Application assumed MCUboot mode of operation

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_MODE_DIRECT_XIP_WITH_REVERT
symbols.prompt: MCUboot has been configured for DirectXIP with revert
symbols.help:
MCUboot expects slot0_partition and slot1_partition to exist in DT.
In this mode MCUboot will boot the application with the higher version
from either slot, as long as it has been marked to be boot
next time for test or permanently. In case when application is marked
for test it needs to confirm itself, on the first boot, or it will
be removed and MCUboot will revert to booting previously approved
application.
This mode does not allow freely switching between application
versions, as, once higher version application is approved, it is
not possible to select lower version for boot.
This mode selects MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_NO_DOWNGRADE as it is not possible
to downgrade running application, but note that MCUboot may do that
if application with higher version will not get confirmed.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Modules > MCUboot bootloader support > On board MCUboot operation mode > Application assumed MCUboot mode of operation

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_MODE_FIRMWARE_UPDATER
symbols.prompt: MCUboot has been configured in firmware updater mode
symbols.help:
MCUboot will only boot slot0_partition for the main application but has
an entrance mechanism defined for entering the slot1_partition which is
a dedicated firmware updater application used to update the slot0_partition
application.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Modules > MCUboot bootloader support > On board MCUboot operation mode > Application assumed MCUboot mode of operation

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_MODE_HAS_NO_DOWNGRADE
symbols.help:
Selected mode supports downgrade prevention, where you cannot switch to
an application with lower version than the currently running application.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Modules > MCUboot bootloader support > On board MCUboot operation mode

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_MODE_OVERWRITE_ONLY
symbols.prompt: MCUboot has been configured to just overwrite primary slot
symbols.help:
MCUboot will take contents of secondary slot of an image and will
overwrite primary slot with it.
In this mode it is not possible to revert back to previous version
as it is not stored in the secondary slot.
This mode supports MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_NO_DOWNGRADE which means
that the overwrite will not happen unless the version of secondary
slot is higher than the version in primary slot.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Modules > MCUboot bootloader support > On board MCUboot operation mode > Application assumed MCUboot mode of operation

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_MODE_RAM_LOAD
symbols.prompt: MCUboot has been configured for RAM LOAD operation
symbols.help:
MCUboot expects slot0_partition and slot1_partition to exist in DT. In this mode, MCUboot
will select the image with the higher version number, copy it to RAM and begin execution
from there. The image must be linked to execute from RAM, the address that it is copied
to is specified using the load-addr argument when running imgtool.
This option automatically selects MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_NO_DOWNGRADE as it is not possible
to swap back to older version of the application.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Modules > MCUboot bootloader support > On board MCUboot operation mode > Application assumed MCUboot mode of operation

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_MODE_RAM_LOAD_WITH_REVERT
symbols.prompt: MCUboot has been configured for RAM LOAD with revert
symbols.help:
MCUboot expects slot0_partition and slot1_partition to exist in DT. In this mode, MCUboot
will select the image with the higher version number, copy it to RAM and begin execution
from there. The image must be linked to execute from RAM, the address that it is copied
to is specified using the load-addr argument when running imgtool.
This option automatically selects MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_NO_DOWNGRADE as
MCUBoot will automatically select the highest revision of the application
to boot. Note however that MCUBoot will select an older revision of
the application if the booted revision does not mark itself as confirmed.
In this mode MCUboot will boot the application with the higher
version from either slot, as long as it has been marked to be boot
next time for test or permanently. In case when application is marked
for test it needs to confirm itself, on the first boot, or it will be
removed and MCUboot will revert to booting previously approved
application. Note that in this mode MCUboot will not boot an
application if it does not have an image header, so if an application
is flashed manually it should be marked as confirmed
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Modules > MCUboot bootloader support > On board MCUboot operation mode > Application assumed MCUboot mode of operation

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_MODE_SINGLE_APP
symbols.prompt: MCUboot has been configured for single slot execution
symbols.help:
MCUboot will only boot slot0_partition placed application and does
not care about other slots. In this mode application is not able
to DFU its own update to secondary slot and all updates need to
be performed using MCUboot serial recovery.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Modules > MCUboot bootloader support > On board MCUboot operation mode > Application assumed MCUboot mode of operation

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_MODE_SINGLE_APP_RAM_LOAD
symbols.prompt: MCUboot has been configured in single app RAM load mode
symbols.help:
MCUboot can load the image to RAM from an arbitrary location. In this mode,
MCUboot will copy the image to RAM and begin execution from there. The image
must be linked to execute from RAM, the address that it is copied to is
specified using the load-addr argument when running imgtool.
Note that while not used directly, a slot0_partition must be defined in the
DT, as it is used to get information about size of the image to be loaded.
This option automatically selects MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_NO_DOWNGRADE as it is
not possible to swap back to older version of the application. In fact, none
of the swap operations are supported in this mode.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Modules > MCUboot bootloader support > On board MCUboot operation mode > Application assumed MCUboot mode of operation

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_MODE_SWAP_SCRATCH
symbols.prompt: MCUboot has been configured for swap using scratch operation
symbols.help:
MCUboot expects slot0_partition, slot1_partition and scratch_partition
to be present in DT, and application will boot from slot0_partition.
In this mode scratch_partition is used as temporary storage when
MCUboot swaps application from the secondary slot to the primary
slot.
MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_NO_DOWNGRADE should also be selected
if MCUboot has been built with MCUBOOT_DOWNGRADE_PREVENTION.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Modules > MCUboot bootloader support > On board MCUboot operation mode > Application assumed MCUboot mode of operation

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_MODE_SWAP_USING_MOVE
symbols.prompt: MCUboot has been configured for swap using move operation
symbols.help:
MCUboot expects slot0_partition and slot1_partition to be present
in DT and application will boot from slot0_partition.
MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_NO_DOWNGRADE should also be selected
if MCUboot has been built with MCUBOOT_DOWNGRADE_PREVENTION.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Modules > MCUboot bootloader support > On board MCUboot operation mode > Application assumed MCUboot mode of operation

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_MODE_SWAP_USING_OFFSET
symbols.prompt: MCUboot has been configured for swap using offset operation
symbols.help:
MCUboot expects slot0_partition and slot1_partition to be present
in DT and application will boot from slot0_partition.
MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_NO_DOWNGRADE should also be selected
if MCUboot has been built with MCUBOOT_DOWNGRADE_PREVENTION.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Modules > MCUboot bootloader support > On board MCUboot operation mode > Application assumed MCUboot mode of operation

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_BOOTLOADER_MODE_SWAP_WITHOUT_SCRATCH
symbols.prompt: MCUboot has been configured for swap without scratch operation [DEPRECATED]

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE
symbols.prompt: Path to the mcuboot encryption key file
symbols.help:
The file contains the public key that is used to encrypt the
ephemeral key that encrypts the image. The corresponding
private key is hard coded in the MCUboot source code and is
used to decrypt the ephemeral key that is embedded in the
image. The file is in PEM format.

If set to a non-empty value, the build system tries to
sign and encrypt the final binaries using a 'west sign -t imgtool'
command. The binaries are placed in the build directory at
zephyr/zephyr.signed.encrypted.bin and
zephyr/zephyr.signed.encrypted.hex.

The file names can be customized with CONFIG_KERNEL_BIN_NAME.
The existence of bin and hex files depends on CONFIG_BUILD_OUTPUT_BIN
and CONFIG_BUILD_OUTPUT_HEX.

This option should either be an absolute path or a path relative to
the west workspace topdir.
Example: './bootloader/mcuboot/enc-rsa2048-pub.pem'

If left empty, you must encrypt the Zephyr binaries manually.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Modules > MCUboot bootloader support

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_EXTRA_IMGTOOL_ARGS

symbols.help:
When signing (CONFIG_MCUBOOT_SIGNATURE_KEY_FILE is a non-empty
string) you can use this option to pass extra options to
imgtool. For example, you could set this to "--version 1.2".
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Modules > MCUboot bootloader support

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_GENERATE_CONFIRMED_IMAGE

symbols.help:
The signed, padded, and confirmed binaries are placed in the build
directory at zephyr/zephyr.signed.confirmed.bin and
zephyr/zephyr.signed.confirmed.hex.

The file names can be customized with CONFIG_KERNEL_BIN_NAME.
The existence of bin and hex files depends on CONFIG_BUILD_OUTPUT_BIN
and CONFIG_BUILD_OUTPUT_HEX.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Modules > MCUboot bootloader support

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_GENERATE_UNSIGNED_IMAGE
symbols.prompt: Generate unsigned binary image bootable with MCUboot
symbols.help:
Enabling this configuration allows automatic unsigned binary image
generation when MCUboot signing key is not provided,
i.e., MCUBOOT_SIGNATURE_KEY_FILE is left empty. A hash of the
image will be generated and included in the unsigned image, instead
of a signature.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Modules > MCUboot bootloader support

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_IMGTOOL_OVERWRITE_ONLY

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_IMGTOOL_SIGN_VERSION

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_IMGTOOL_UUID_CID_NAME
symbols.help:
The image class unique identifier.
The following formats are supported:
 - Image class name (i.e. nRF5340_door_lock_btperipheral).
   This format requires MCUBOOT_IMGTOOL_UUID_VID_NAME to be defined
   as the VID UUID is used as the namespace for image class UUID.
 - Raw UUID (i.e. 12345678-1234-5678-1234-567812345678)
 - Raw HEX UUID (i.e. 12345678123456781234567812345678)
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Modules > MCUboot bootloader support > Append image class unique identifier TLV

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_IMGTOOL_UUID_VID

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_IMGTOOL_UUID_VID_NAME
symbols.help:
The vendor unique identifier.
The following formats are supported:
 - Domain name (i.e. amce.corp)

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUBOOT_SIGNATURE_KEY_FILE
symbols.prompt: Path to the mcuboot signing key file
symbols.help:
The file contains a key pair whose public half is verified
by your target's MCUboot image. The file is in PEM format.

If set to a non-empty value, the build system tries to
sign the final binaries using a 'west sign -t imgtool' command.
The signed binaries are placed in the build directory
at zephyr/zephyr.signed.bin and zephyr/zephyr.signed.hex.

The file names can be customized with CONFIG_KERNEL_BIN_NAME.
The existence of bin and hex files depends on CONFIG_BUILD_OUTPUT_BIN
and CONFIG_BUILD_OUTPUT_HEX.

This option should contain a path to the same file as the
BOOT_SIGNATURE_KEY_FILE option in your MCUboot .config. The path
may be absolute or relative to the west workspace topdir. (The MCUboot
config option is used for the MCUboot bootloader image; this option is
for your application which is to be loaded by MCUboot. The MCUboot
config option can be a relative path from the MCUboot repository
root.)

If left empty and MCUBOOT_GENERATE_UNSIGNED_IMAGE is not set, you
must sign and prepare the Zephyr binaries manually to be bootable
from MCUboot.

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_FS
symbols.help:
Enables MCUmgr handlers for file management

Note: This option allows MCUmgr clients to access anything in the file system, including
application-stored secrets like private keys. Use of this feature in production without
adequate protection mechanisms is strongly discouraged (applications can enable
MCUMGR_GRP_FS_FILE_ACCESS_HOOK and register to receive callbacks when file access is
attempted, which they can then filter, allow, deny or rewrite paths).
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_FS_CHECKSUM_HASH
symbols.help:
Enable this to support the hash/checksum MCUmgr functionality, individual checksum and
hash types need to be enabled below. Note that this requires enough stack space to buffer
data from the file being read and generate the output hash/checksum.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for file management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_FS_CHECKSUM_HASH_CHUNK_SIZE
symbols.help: Chunk size of buffer to use when calculating file checksum or hash (uses stack).
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for file management > Checksum/hash MCUmgr functions

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_FS_CHECKSUM_HASH_SUPPORTED_CMD
symbols.help:

and checksum types that can be used.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for file management > Checksum/hash MCUmgr functions

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_FS_CHECKSUM_HASH_SUPPORTED_MAX_TYPES
symbols.prompt: Predicted maximum number of types to return on supported list
symbols.help:
This is used for defining CBOR map holding supported hash/checksum info. The value does
not affect memory allocation, it is used by zcbor to figure out how to encode map
depending on its predicted size.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for file management > Checksum/hash MCUmgr functions > Supported hash/checksum command

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_FS_DL_CHUNK_SIZE
symbols.prompt: Maximum chunk size for file downloads
symbols.help:
Sets the MAXIMUM size of chunk which will be rounded down to number of bytes that, with
all the required headers, will fit into MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_NETBUF_SIZE. This means that
actual value might be lower then selected, in which case compiler warning will be issued.
Look inside fs_mgmt_config.h for details. Note that header sizes are affected by
MCUMGR_GRP_FS_MAX_OFFSET_LEN.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for file management > Setting custom size of download file chunk

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_FS_DL_CHUNK_SIZE_LIMIT
symbols.prompt: Setting custom size of download file chunk
symbols.help:
By default file chunk, that will be read off storage and fit into MCUmgr frame, is
automatically calculated to fit into buffer of size MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_NETBUF_SIZE with
all headers. Enabling this option allows to set MAXIMUM value that will be allowed for
such chunk. Look inside fs_mgmt_config.h for details.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for file management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_FS_FILE_ACCESS_HOOK
symbols.help:
Allows applications to control file access (e.g. for uploading and downloading of files)
by registering for a callback which is then triggered whenever a files are accessed
using the FS management group function. This also, optionally, allows re-writing or
changing of supplied file paths. Note that this may be called multiple times for each
file read and write due to MCUmgr's method of operation with a single file state.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for file management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_FS_FILE_AUTOMATIC_IDLE_CLOSE_TIME
symbols.help:

up. Each access to the file will reset the idle time to 0.

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_FS_FILE_SEMAPHORE_TAKE_TIME

command is used. If unable to acquire the semaphore, then MGMT_ERR_EBUSY will be

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_FS_MAX_FILE_SIZE
symbols.prompt: Maximum file size that could be uploaded/downloaded

Maximum file size that will be allowed to be downloaded from device. This option decides
on number of bytes that are reserved in CBOR frame for storage of offset/size of file
downloaded.

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_FS_MAX_FILE_SIZE_4GB

symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for file management > Maximum file size that could be uploaded/downloaded

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_FS_MAX_FILE_SIZE_64KB

frame with file chunk.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for file management > Maximum file size that could be uploaded/downloaded

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_FS_MAX_OFFSET_LEN
symbols.help:
Maximal byte length of encoded offset/size, within transferred CBOR frame containing
chunk of downloaded file. This value affects how much of data will fit into download
buffer, as it selects sizes of fields within headers.

Note: This option is hidden intentionally as it is intended to be assigned from limited
set of allowed values, depending on the selection made in MCUMGR_GRP_FS_MAX_FILE_SIZE
menu.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for file management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_FS_PATH_LEN
symbols.help:
Limits the maximum path length for file operations, in bytes. A buffer of this size gets
allocated on the stack during handling of file upload and download commands.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for file management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG
symbols.help: Enables MCUmgr handlers for image management
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_ALLOW_CONFIRM_NON_ACTIVE_IMAGE_ANY
symbols.prompt: Allow to confirm slots of non-active image
symbols.help:
Allows to confirm any slot of non-active image. Normally it should not be allowed to
confirm any slots of non-active image, via MCUmgr commands, to prevent confirming
something that is broken and may not boot in other slot; instead application should have
a means to test and confirm the image.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for image management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_ALLOW_CONFIRM_NON_ACTIVE_IMAGE_SECONDARY
symbols.prompt: Allow to confirm secondary slot of non-active image
symbols.help:
Allows to confirm secondary (non-active) slot of non-active image. Normally it should not
be allowed to confirm any slots of non-active image, via MCUmgr commands, to prevent
confirming something that is broken and may not boot in other slot; instead application
should have a means to test and confirm the image.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for image management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_ALLOW_CONFIRM_NON_ACTIVE_SLOT
symbols.prompt: Allow to confirm non-active slots of any image
symbols.help:
Allows to confirm non-active slot of any image. Normally it should not be allowed to
confirm any slots via MCUmgr commands, to prevent confirming something that is broken
and was not verified to boot correctly. Option is always enabled when in overwrite only
mode, because updates are permanent and using the confirm flag is the intended method for
updates.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for image management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_ALLOW_ERASE_PENDING
symbols.help:
Allows erasing secondary slot which is marked for test or confirmed; this allows erasing
slots that have been set for next boot but the device has not reset yet, so have not yet
been swapped.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for image management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_DIRECT_UPLOAD
symbols.help:
Enables directly uploading image to selected image partition. This changes how "image" is
understood by MCUmgr: normally MCUmgr allows uploading to the first slot of the only
image it knows, where image is understood as two slots (two DTS images for Zephyr); this
allows to treat every DTS defined image as direct target for upload, and more than two
may be used (4 at this time).

Note: When direct upload is used the image numbers are shifted by + 1, and the default
behaviour is, when image is not selected, to upload to image that represents secondary
slot in normal operation.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for image management

symbols.prompt: MCUmgr reset or upload command timeout
symbols.help: Change default value when platform needs a different time.

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_FRUGAL_LIST
symbols.prompt: Omit zero, empty or false values from status list
symbols.help:
The status list send back from the device will only be filled with data that is non-zero,
non-empty or true. This option slightly reduces number of bytes transferred back from
a device but requires support in client software, which has to default omitted values.
Works correctly with the go mcumgr-cli application.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for image management

allocation, it is used by zcbor to figure out how to encode map depending on its
predicted size.

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_MUTEX
symbols.help:
This will enable use of a mutex to lock the image group object access, preventing issues
of concurrent thread (i.e. multiple transport) access. This option also makes the
``img_mgmt_reset_upload()`` function visible in the image management group header, which
can be used by applications to reset the image management state (useful if there are
multiple ways that firmware updates can be loaded).
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for image management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_REJECT_DIRECT_XIP_MISMATCHED_SLOT
symbols.prompt: Reject Direct-XIP applications with mismatched address
symbols.help:
When enabled, the MCUmgr will compare base address of application, encoded into .bin
file header with use of imgtool, on upload and will reject binaries that would not be
able to start from available Direct-XIP address. The base address can be set, to an image
binary header, with imgtool, using the --rom-fixed command line option.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for image management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_SLOT_INFO
symbols.help:
This will enable the slot information function which will return information about all
images and slots that the application can see.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for image management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_SLOT_INFO_HOOKS
symbols.help:
This will enable the slot info function hooks which can be used to add additional
information to responses.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for image management > Slot info

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_STATUS_HOOKS
symbols.help:
This will enable DFU status hooks which can be checked by the application to monitor DFU
uploads. Note that these are status checking only, to allow inspecting of a file upload
or prevent it, CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_UPLOAD_CHECK_HOOK must be used.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for image management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_TOO_LARGE_BOOTLOADER_INFO
symbols.help: Will fetch the maximum image size from the bootloader info retention subsystem module.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for image management > Image size check overhead

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_TOO_LARGE_CHECK
symbols.help:
MCUboot images should be limited to the maximum size that the bootloader can swap, in
order to know this size, additional information is needed from the MCUboot
configuration, otherwise an image can be uploaded that is too large for the bootloader
to swap, this selects which method to use.

Note: setting this to a non-disabled option will prevent uploading of padded and
confirmed images, if support for that is required then this feature should be left as
disabled.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for image management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_TOO_LARGE_DISABLED
symbols.help: Will not take MCUboot configuration into account when checking for maximum file size.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for image management > Image size check overhead

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_TOO_LARGE_SYSBUILD
symbols.help: Will use the image overhead size calculated during Sysbuild image configuration.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for image management > Image size check overhead

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_UPDATABLE_IMAGE_NUMBER
symbols.help:
Sets how many application images are supported (pairs of secondary and primary slots).
Setting this to 2 requires MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_NETBUF_SIZE to be at least 512b.

Note: The UPDATEABLE_IMAGE_NUMBER of MCUBOOT configuration, even for Zephyr build,
needs to be set to the same value; this is due to the fact that the MCUmgr uses
boot_util and the UPDATEABLE_IMAGE_NUMBER controls number of images supported
by that library.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for image management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_UPLOAD_CHECK_HOOK
symbols.help:
This will enable the upload check hook which will send image upload requests to
registered callbacks to check with the user application if an upload should be accepted
or rejected.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for image management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_UPLOAD_DATA_ALIGNMENT_SIZE
symbols.help: Change default value when platform needs different data alignment.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr client handlers for image management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_USE_HEAP_FOR_FLASH_IMG_CONTEXT
symbols.prompt: Use heap mem pool for flash image DFU context
symbols.help:
Use heap to allocate flash image upload context, otherwise a static variable will
be used. The context object is used by MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_MANAGER to buffer image writes
and has significant size, mainly affected by image write buffer of
the CONFIG_IMG_BLOCK_BUF_SIZE size and additional fields that hold the state information
(struct flash_img_context).
When the option is not enabled it increases static RAM use.
Make sure with testing, when enabling the option, that the heap has enough size
to allocate this context or it will not be possible to perform DFU; it may also not be
possible to allocate such context when heap is under pressure, due to application
operation, an issue that should also be addressed within application.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for image management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_VERBOSE_ERR
symbols.prompt: Verbose error responses when uploading application image
symbols.help: Add additional "rsn" key to SMP responses, where provided, explaining non-0 "rc" codes.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for image management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_IMG_VERSION_CMP_USE_BUILD_NUMBER
symbols.prompt: Use build number while comparing image version
symbols.help:
By default, the image version comparison relies only on version major, minor and
revision. Enable this option to take into account the build number as well.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for image management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_OS_INFO_HARDWARE_INFO_SHORT_HARDWARE_PLATFORM
symbols.help:
Will use the board name and board revision without the SoC or variant information if
enabled which is the Zephyr 4.2 and earlier behaviour, otherwise will output the full
board target for the hardware platform.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for OS management > Support for info command

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_OS_INFO_MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE
symbols.prompt: Maximum response size for info command
symbols.help:

size to store the data in. If the output response is too big then the output will not be

on the device, including sizes, free space and minimum amount of free space.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for OS management

symbols.help:
Response will not include the "blksiz" field which Zephyr does not support (as it has a
value of 1). Enable this if your client software is able to process "mpstat" response
without the "blksiz" field for each memory pool. Enabling this option will slightly
reduce code size.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for OS management > Support for memory pool statistics command

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_OS_RESET_BOOT_MODE
symbols.help:
Allows applications to set the boot mode using the retention boot mode module which
allows for booting other images e.g. as part of a bootloader. This is done with an
optional field in the reset command which specifies the value of the boot mode.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for OS management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_OS_RESET_HOOK
symbols.help:
Allows applications to control and get notifications of when a reset command has been
issued via an MCUmgr command. With this option disabled, modules will reboot when the
command is received without notification, when this is enabled and a handler is
registered, the application will be notified that a reset command has been received and
will allow the application to perform any required operations before accepting or
declining the reset request.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for OS management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_OS_RESET_MS
symbols.help:
When a reset command is received, the system waits this many milliseconds before
performing the reset. This delay allows time for the MCUmgr response to be delivered.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for OS management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_OS_TASKSTAT_MAX_NUM_THREADS

Response will not include fields the Zephyr does not collect statistic for. Enable this
if your client software is able to process "taskstat" response that would be missing
"runtime", "cswcnt", "last_checkin" and "next_checkin" map entries for each listed task.
Enabling this option will slightly reduce code size.

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_OS_TASKSTAT_SIGNED_PRIORITY
symbols.help:
Zephyr uses int8_t as thread priorities, but in taskstat response it encodes them as
unsigned. Enabling this option will use signed int for priorities in responses, which is
more natural for Zephyr. Disable this option if your client software is unable to
properly decode and accept signed integers as priorities.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for OS management > Support for taskstat command

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_OS_TASKSTAT_STACK_INFO
symbols.prompt: Include stack info in taskstat responses
symbols.help:
Enabling this option adds stack information into "taskstat" command responses, this is
default when THREAD_STACK_INFO is selected. Disable this option only when your client
application is able to process "taskstat" response without the "stksiz" and "stkuse"
fields. It is worth disabling this option when THREAD_STACK_INFO is disabled, as it will
prevent sending zeroed stack information just to fill all the fields in "taskstat"
responses, and it will slightly reduce code size.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for OS management > Support for taskstat command

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_OS_TASKSTAT_THREAD_NAME_LEN

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_SETTINGS_BUFFER_TYPE_STACK

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_SETTINGS_NAME_LEN

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_SETTINGS_VALUE_LEN

the stack or the allocated size of the variable if placed on the heap (settings does not

symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers > MCUmgr handlers for settings management

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_SHELL
symbols.help:
Enables MCUmgr handlers for shell management. The handler will utilize the dummy backend
to execute shell commands and capture the output to an internal memory buffer. This way,
there is no interaction with physical interfaces outside of the scope of the user. It is
possible to use additional shell backends in coordination with this handler and they will
not interfere. The CONFIG_SHELL_BACKEND_DUMMY_BUF_SIZE Kconfig will affect how many
characters will be returned from command output, if your output gets cut, then increase
the value. Remember to set MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_NETBUF_SIZE accordingly. Note that maximum
length of shell command accepted is regulated by the CONFIG_SHELL_CMD_BUFF_SIZE, and a
buffer for a command is allocated on a stack, by the MCUmgr, so enabling MCUMGR_GRP_SHELL
and changes to the CONFIG_SHELL_CMD_BUFF_SIZE may increase stack size requirements.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Command Handlers

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_GRP_SHELL_LEGACY_RC_RETURN_CODE
symbols.prompt: Legacy behaviour: Use rc field for shell function return code
symbols.help:
Enabling this options brings back legacy behaviour where the shell return code is
returned, incorrectly, in the rc field that was originally designated for returning SMP
processing errors. When disabled, there will be an additional ret field which contains
the shell command exit code, and rc will be used for SMP processing error codes.

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_MGMT_NOTIFICATION_HOOKS
symbols.help:
With this enabled, applications and parts of code can register for MCUmgr event
notifications which will result in callbacks when a registered event occurs. Note that
this enables the base notification functionality but itself does not enable any
notifications, which must be enabled by selecting other Kconfig options.

To enable notifications in code, mgmt_callback_register() must be called with the
callback function and events that want to be received. Multiple handlers can be
registered and will all be called when registered events occur.

Some callbacks support notifying the calling function of a status, in which to accept
or decline the current operation, by returning false this will signal to the calling
function that the request should be denied, for informal-only notifications or
acceptable, true must be returned by all the registered notification handlers.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_SMP_CBOR_MAX_DECODING_LEVELS
symbols.prompt: Number of map/list encapsulations allowed for SMP decoding
symbols.help:
This is a maximum number of levels of maps/lists that will be expected to be decoded
within different command groups. SMP commands/groups that provide no CBOR encoded payload
have no requirements. Commands that provide CBOR payload require at least 1 level, and
additional levels for each map/list encapsulation. For example if command accepts payload
of map of parameters it will need 2 levels. This number translates to zcbor backup states,
it increases size of cbor_nb_reader structure by zcbor_state_t size per one unit selected
here.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_SMP_CBOR_MAX_ENCODING_LEVELS
symbols.prompt: Number of map/list encapsulations allowed for SMP encoding
symbols.help:
This is a maximum number of levels of maps/lists that will be encoded within different
commmand groups. This number translates to zcbor backup states, it increases size of
cbor_nb_writer structure by zcbor_state_t size per one unit selected here.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_SMP_CBOR_MAX_MAIN_MAP_ENTRIES
symbols.prompt: Number of predicted maximum entries to main response map
symbols.help:
This is number of predicted entries in main response map, the one that encapsulates
everything within response. This value is used by zcbor to predict needed map encoding,
and does not affect memory allocation or usage. Builtin command processors rarely add
large amounts of data directly to main map, creating sub-maps instead so the default
value works fine with them. If your app directly adds fields to main map, without
encapsulating them, you may want to increase this value in case when encoding starts to
fail.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_SMP_CBOR_MIN_DECODING_LEVELS
symbols.help:
Minimal decoding levels, map/list encapsulation, required to be supported by zcbor
decoding of SMP responses is auto generated from MCUMGR_SMP_CBOR_MIN_DECODING_LEVEL_?
options. A group or command that adds additional maps/lists above the base map, which is
already taken into account, should select one of the MCUMGR_SMP_CBOR_MIN_DECODING_LEVEL_?.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support
