symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_SMP_COMMAND_STATUS_HOOKS
symbols.help:
This will enable SMP command status notification hooks for when an SMP message is
received or processed.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_SMP_LEGACY_RC_BEHAVIOUR
symbols.help:
This will enable legacy result code response behaviour of having rc present in responses
when the status is 0. With this option disabled, MCUmgr acts with new behaviour and will
only return rc is the result code is non-zero (i.e. an error occurred).

If a command only returns a result code, this will mean that the response will be empty
with the new behaviour enabled, as opposed to the old behaviour where the rc field will
be present in the response.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Support original protocol

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_SMP_SUPPORT_ORIGINAL_PROTOCOL
symbols.help:
This option will enable supporting the original SMP protocol whereby all errors are
returned in the "rc" field as well as the new protocol whereby there is a dedicated
entry for command error/result codes. The protocol selection is indicated by the request
header sent by the client.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_SMP_VERBOSE_ERR_RESPONSE
symbols.help:
Support for encoding "rc" code explanation in form of "rsn" text string. This is useful,
when returning MGMT_ERR_EUNKNOWN, to add additional information on the source of an
error. Note that the "rsn" is string additional to "rc" code, so
MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_NETBUF_SIZE should be large enough to be able to encode both.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Support original protocol

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_BT
symbols.help: Enables handling of SMP commands received over Bluetooth.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_BT_CONN_PARAM_CONTROL
symbols.prompt: Request specific connection parameters for SMP packet exchange
symbols.help:
Enables support for requesting specific connection parameters when SMP commands are
handled. This option allows to speed up the command exchange process.
It is recommended to enable this if SMP is used for DFU.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Bluetooth MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_BT_CONN_PARAM_CONTROL_LATENCY
symbols.prompt: Peripheral latency for SMP packet exchange
symbols.help: Peripheral latency in Connection Intervals used during the exchange of SMP packets.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Bluetooth MCUmgr SMP transport > Request specific connection parameters for SMP packet exchange

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_BT_CONN_PARAM_CONTROL_MAX_INT
symbols.prompt: Maximum connection interval for SMP packet exchange
symbols.help: Maximum connection interval in 1.25ms units used during the exchange of SMP packets.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Bluetooth MCUmgr SMP transport > Request specific connection parameters for SMP packet exchange

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_BT_CONN_PARAM_CONTROL_MIN_INT
symbols.prompt: Minimum connection interval for SMP packet exchange
symbols.help: Minimum connection interval in 1.25ms units used during the exchange of SMP packets.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Bluetooth MCUmgr SMP transport > Request specific connection parameters for SMP packet exchange

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_BT_CONN_PARAM_CONTROL_RESTORE_TIME
symbols.prompt: Connection parameters restore time in milliseconds
symbols.help:
The value is a time of inactivity on the SMP characteristic after which connection
parameters are restored to peripheral preferred values (BT_GAP_PERIPHERAL_PREF_PARAMS).
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Bluetooth MCUmgr SMP transport > Request specific connection parameters for SMP packet exchange

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_BT_CONN_PARAM_CONTROL_RETRY_TIME
symbols.prompt: Connection parameters update retry time in milliseconds
symbols.help:
In case connection parameters update fails due to an error, this option specifies the
time of the next update attempt.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Bluetooth MCUmgr SMP transport > Request specific connection parameters for SMP packet exchange

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_BT_CONN_PARAM_CONTROL_TIMEOUT
symbols.prompt: Supervision timeout for SMP packet exchange
symbols.help: Supervision timeout in 10ms used during the exchange of SMP packets.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Bluetooth MCUmgr SMP transport > Request specific connection parameters for SMP packet exchange

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_BT_DYNAMIC_SVC_REGISTRATION
symbols.help:
When enabled, the SMP service will be automatically registered at boot time and can then
be dynamically registered/unregistered using a dedicated API. Otherwise, the SMP service
will be statically defined and registered.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Bluetooth MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_BT_PERM
symbols.prompt: Permission used for the SMP service
symbols.help: Permission settings for GATT characteristics of the SMP service.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Bluetooth MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_BT_PERM_RW
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Bluetooth MCUmgr SMP transport > Permission used for the SMP service

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_BT_PERM_RW_AUTHEN
symbols.prompt: Require encryption and authentication for access
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Bluetooth MCUmgr SMP transport > Permission used for the SMP service

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_BT_PERM_RW_ENCRYPT
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Bluetooth MCUmgr SMP transport > Permission used for the SMP service

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_BT_REASSEMBLY
symbols.prompt: Reassemble packets in Bluetooth SMP transport
symbols.help:
When enabled, the SMP BT transport will buffer and reassemble received packet fragments
before passing it for further processing.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Bluetooth MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_DUMMY
symbols.help:
Enables the dummy SMP backend which can be used for unit testing SMP functionality
without needing a real interface or driver.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_DUMMY_RX_BUF_SIZE
symbols.prompt: Size of receive buffer for dummy interface mcumgr fragments
symbols.help:
Specifies the size of the MCUmgr dummy backend receive buffer, in bytes. This value
must be large enough to accommodate any line sent by an MCUmgr client.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Dummy SMP backend

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LOG_LEVEL_CHOICE
symbols.prompt: Max compiled-in log level for mcumgr_transport
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LOG_LEVEL_DBG
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Max compiled-in log level for mcumgr_transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LOG_LEVEL_DEFAULT
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Max compiled-in log level for mcumgr_transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LOG_LEVEL_ERR
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Max compiled-in log level for mcumgr_transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LOG_LEVEL_INF
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Max compiled-in log level for mcumgr_transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LOG_LEVEL_OFF
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Max compiled-in log level for mcumgr_transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LOG_LEVEL_WRN
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Max compiled-in log level for mcumgr_transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LORAWAN
symbols.help: Enables handling of SMP commands received over LoRaWAN.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LORAWAN_CONFIRMED_UPLINKS
symbols.help:
Will use confirmed uplink packets for responses if enabled, otherwise will use
unconfirmed packets.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LORAWAN_FRAGMENTED_UPLINKS
symbols.help:
Will fragment messages into multiple uplink messages if they are too big to fit into a
single uplink message. If disabled then uplinks that are too large will not be sent.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LORAWAN_FRAME_PORT
symbols.help:
LoRaWAN download and uplink frame port used for communication. All messages received on
this port will be treated as SMP packets.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LORAWAN_LOG_LEVEL_CHOICE
symbols.prompt: Max compiled-in log level for LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LORAWAN_LOG_LEVEL_DBG
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport > Max compiled-in log level for LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LORAWAN_LOG_LEVEL_DEFAULT
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport > Max compiled-in log level for LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LORAWAN_LOG_LEVEL_ERR
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport > Max compiled-in log level for LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LORAWAN_LOG_LEVEL_INF
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport > Max compiled-in log level for LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LORAWAN_LOG_LEVEL_OFF
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport > Max compiled-in log level for LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LORAWAN_LOG_LEVEL_WRN
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport > Max compiled-in log level for LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LORAWAN_POLL_FOR_DATA
symbols.prompt: Send empty packet if partial packet received
symbols.help:
Will send an empty packet if a partial (fragmented) message has been received from the
server, this will allow the next packet to be received without waiting for next
transmission window.

Note: this requires a dedicated thread in order to prevent blocking the system workqueue.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport > Reassemble LoRaWAN SMP messages

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LORAWAN_POLL_FOR_DATA_RETRIES
symbols.help:
Number of LoRaWAN message send retries if sending fails for the thread for polling for
empty additional packets when a partial frame is received.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport > Reassemble LoRaWAN SMP messages > Send empty packet if partial packet received

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LORAWAN_POLL_FOR_DATA_STACK_SIZE
symbols.help:
Stack size of the thread that will poll for empty additional packets when a partial
frame is received.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport > Reassemble LoRaWAN SMP messages > Send empty packet if partial packet received

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LORAWAN_POLL_FOR_DATA_THREAD_PRIORITY
symbols.help:
Priority of the thread for polling for empty additional packets when a partial frame
is received.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport > Reassemble LoRaWAN SMP messages > Send empty packet if partial packet received

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_LORAWAN_REASSEMBLY
symbols.help:
Will reassemble downlink LoRaWAN messages together to allow for messages larger than a
single message to be received, otherwise will support messages up to a single packet in
size.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > LoRaWAN MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_NETBUF_COUNT
symbols.help:
The number of net_bufs to allocate for MCUmgr. These buffers are used for both requests
and responses.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_NETBUF_MIN_USER_DATA_SIZE
symbols.help: Hidden option to determine minimum user data size.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_NETBUF_SIZE
symbols.help:
The size, in bytes, of each MCUmgr buffer. This value must satisfy the following
relation:
MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_NETBUF_SIZE >= transport-specific-MTU + transport-overhead
In case when MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_SHELL is enabled this value should be set to at least
CONFIG_SHELL_BACKEND_DUMMY_BUF_SIZE + 32.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_NETBUF_USER_DATA_SIZE
symbols.prompt: Size of MCUmgr buffer user data
symbols.help:
The size, in bytes, of user data to allocate for each MCUmgr buffer.

Different MCUmgr transports impose different requirements for this setting. A value of 4
is sufficient for UART and shell, a value of 8 is sufficient for Bluetooth. For UDP, the
userdata must be large enough to hold IPv4/IPv6 addresses.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_RAW_DUMMY
symbols.prompt: Dummy raw UART MCUmgr (non-SMP over console) backend
symbols.help:
Enables the dummy MCUmgr UART backend which does not use SMP over console and does not
have base64 encoding over the data, which can be used for unit testing SMP
functionality without needing a real interface or driver.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_RAW_DUMMY_RX_BUF_SIZE
symbols.prompt: Size of receive buffer for dummy interface MCUmgr fragments
symbols.help:
Specifies the size of the raw MCUmgr dummy backend receive buffer, in bytes. This value
must be large enough to accommodate any line sent by an MCUmgr client.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Dummy raw UART MCUmgr (non-SMP over console) backend

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_RAW_UART
symbols.prompt: Raw UART (non-SMP over console) MCUmgr transport
symbols.help:
Enables handling of MCUmgr commands received over UART, which are not encoded in the SMP
over console format (without additional fields or base64 encoding). This is an even
lighter-weight alternative to CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_UART. It allows MCUmgr commands
to be received over a binary (non-textual) UART without requiring an additional thread.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_RAW_UART_INPUT_TIMEOUT
symbols.help:
If enabled, will time out a partial or erroneous MCUmgr command received via the raw
UART transport after a given time. This prevents the UART from becoming locked if it
never receives the full packet that it was expecting to receive.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Raw UART (non-SMP over console) MCUmgr transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_RAW_UART_INPUT_TIMEOUT_TIME_MS
symbols.help:
Time (in msec) after first receiving data on the UART transport before considering it
as timed out and clearing the receive buffer to await a new command.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Raw UART (non-SMP over console) MCUmgr transport > Input expiration

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_REASSEMBLY
symbols.help: Enable structures and functions needed for packet reassembly by SMP backend.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_SERIAL_HAS_RAW_BINARY_NON_SMP_OVER_CONSOLE
symbols.help:
Hidden Kconfig selected by transports that implement the raw binary non-SMP over console
serial transport and need this functionality to be available in the serial_util.c file.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Common transport configuration

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_SERIAL_HAS_SMP_OVER_CONSOLE
symbols.help:
Hidden Kconfig selected by transports that implement the SMP over console transport and
need this functionality to be available in the serial_util.c file.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Common transport configuration

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_SHELL
symbols.help:
Enables handling of SMP commands received over shell. This allows the shell to be use
for both MCUmgr commands and shell commands.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_SHELL_INPUT_TIMEOUT
symbols.help:
If enabled, will time out a partial or erroneous MCUmgr command received via the shell
transport after a given time. This prevents the shell from becoming locked if it never
receives the full packet that a header indicated it would receive.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Shell MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_SHELL_INPUT_TIMEOUT_TIME
symbols.help:
Time (in msec) after receiving a valid MCUmgr header on the serial transport before
considering it as timed out and returning the shell to normal operation.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Shell MCUmgr SMP transport > Shell input expiration

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_SHELL_MTU
symbols.help:
Maximum size of SMP frames sent and received over shell. This value must satisfy the
following relation:
MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_SHELL_MTU <= MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_NETBUF_SIZE + 2
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Shell MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_SHELL_RX_BUF_COUNT
symbols.help: Number of buffers used for receiving SMP fragments over shell.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Shell MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_UART
symbols.help:
Enables handling of SMP commands received over UART. This is a lightweight alternative
to MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_SHELL. It allows MCUmgr commands to be received over UART without
requiring an additional thread.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_UART_ASYNC
symbols.prompt: Use async UART API when available
symbols.help: The option enables use of UART async API when available for selected MCUmgr UART port.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Common transport configuration

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_UART_ASYNC_BUFS
symbols.prompt: Number of async RX UART buffers
symbols.help:
The asynchronous UART API requires registering RX buffers for received data; when the RX
reaches the end of a buffer, it will send event requesting next buffer, to be able to
receive data without stopping due to running out of buffer space. At least two buffers
area required for smooth RX operation.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Common transport configuration > Use async UART API when available

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_UART_ASYNC_BUF_SIZE
symbols.prompt: Size of single async RX UART buffer
symbols.help: The size of single buffer for asynchronous RX.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > Common transport configuration > Use async UART API when available

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_UART_MTU
symbols.help:
Maximum size of SMP frames sent and received over UART, in bytes. This value must
satisfy the following relation:
MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_UART_MTU <= MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_NETBUF_SIZE + 2
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > UART MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_UDP
symbols.help:
Enables handling of SMP commands received over UDP.
Will start a thread for listening on the configured UDP port.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_UDP_AUTOMATIC_INIT
symbols.help:
Enable starting the UDP SMP transport at boot time without needing any code in the
application to do this, otherwise will need the user application to manually start and
stop the transport using `smp_udp_open` and `smp_udp_close`.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > UDP MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_UDP_DTLS
symbols.help:
Enable DTLS for UDP transport, this means normal non-authenticated connections will not
be supported and the transport will not be started automatically at boot-up, the
application will need to add the certificates to the system and set them up before
opening the transport using the `smp_udp_open` function.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > UDP MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_UDP_DTLS_TLS_TAG
symbols.help:
The TLS tag which the application must add the certificates to before starting the UDP
transport.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > UDP MCUmgr SMP transport > DTLS

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_UDP_IPV4
symbols.help:
Enable SMP UDP using IPv4 addressing.
Can be enabled alongside IPv6 addressing.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > UDP MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_UDP_IPV6
symbols.help:
Enable SMP UDP using IPv6 addressing.
Can be enabled alongside IPv4 addressing.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > UDP MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_UDP_MTU
symbols.help:
Maximum size of SMP frames sent and received over UDP, in bytes.
This value must satisfy the following relation:
MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_UDP_MTU <= MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_NETBUF_SIZE + SMP msg overhead - address size
where address size is determined by IPv4/IPv6 selection.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > UDP MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_UDP_PORT
symbols.help: UDP port that SMP server will listen for SMP commands on.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > UDP MCUmgr SMP transport

symbols.name: CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_UDP_STACK_SIZE
symbols.help: Stack size of the SMP UDP listening thread
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Device Management > MCUmgr Support > Transports and Transport Related Configuration Options > UDP MCUmgr SMP transport

configure it here. In order for PXP flip to work, calls to

and height (without flip applied).  Note that the width and
height settings of the screen in devicetree should not be modified
from their values in the default screen orientation when using this
functionality.

count, the hardware may not have enough time to process it.

It will listen well-known address ff02::fb and 224.0.0.251.

You must set CONFIG_NET_HOSTNAME to some meaningful value and
then mDNS will start to respond to <hostname>.local mDNS queries.

processes PTR, SRV, and TXT records according to RFC 6763.

using e.g. 'avahi-browse -t -r _greybus._tcp'.

symbols.name: CONFIG_MDNS_RESPONDER_DNS_SD_SERVICE_TYPE_ENUMERATION

performs DNS-SD Service Type Enumeration according to RFC 6763,
Chapter 9. By doing so, Zephyr network services are discoverable
using e.g. 'avahi-browse -t -r _services._dns-sd._udp.local'.

struct to keep track of the threads associated with this
particular memory domain.

symbols.name: CONFIG_MEM_DOMAIN_ISOLATED_STACKS
symbols.help:
If enabled, thread stacks within the same memory domains are
isolated which means threads within the same memory domains
have no access to others threads' stacks.

If disabled, threads within the same memory domains can access
other threads' stacks.

Regardless of this settings, threads cannot access the stacks of
threads outside of their domains.

symbols.name: CONFIG_MIN_HEAP
symbols.help:
Enable support for a generic Min-Heap data structure library.

A Min-Heap is a binary tree-based data structure in which the
smallest element is always at the root. It supports efficient
insertion and removal of the minimum element in O(log n) time,
making it useful for priority queues, schedulers, and timeout
queues.

This implementation is designed for general-purpose use in both
kernel and application code. It supports static and dynamic
initialization and allows for custom comparator functions.

Note: This is unrelated to the kernel's heap memory allocator
(used for dynamic memory allocation with `k_malloc()` or
`k_heap_alloc()`). The "heap" in Min-Heap refers to the ordering
structure, not memory management.

symbols.name: CONFIG_MODEM_BACKEND_UART_ISR_RECEIVE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS
symbols.prompt: Modem ISR UART delay between first byte received and RECEIVE_READY pipe event
symbols.help:
This defines the delay, in milliseconds, that the backend waits
when receiving a byte before sending the RECEIVE_READY pipe event.
The backend will anyway send the event before this delay if buffer space runs out.
A good value is ~90% the time it takes to fill half the receive buffer.
It can be calculated as follows:
(<UART receive_buf_size> / 2) / (<UART baud rate> / <UART bits per byte>) * <ms per sec>
By default (for the modem_cellular driver): (512 / 2) / (115200 / 10) * 1000 = 22,222 => 20
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Modem modules > Modem UART backend module

symbols.name: CONFIG_MODEM_CELLULAR
symbols.help:
This driver uses the generic 3gpp AT commands, along
with the standard protocols CMUX and PPP, to configure
cellular modems to establish a point-to-point
network connection. It is a template for tailored
drivers for the ublox, quectel and other modems, which
include power management and more complex device specific
features.

symbols.name: CONFIG_MODEM_CMD_HANDLER
symbols.help:
This generic command handler uses a modem interface to process
incoming data and hand it back to the modem driver via callbacks
defined for:
- modem responses
- unsolicited messages
- specified handlers for current operation
To configure this layer for use, create a modem_cmd_handler_data
object and pass it's reference to modem_cmd_handler_init() along with
the modem_cmd_handler reference from your modem_context object.

symbols.name: CONFIG_MODEM_CMUX_MSC_FC_THRESHOLD
symbols.prompt: Enable flow control when the DLCI ring buffer has less than this many bytes free
symbols.help:
When the available space in a DLCI receive ring buffer is less than this
value, the CMUX module will send Modem Status Command frame with the
flow control bit set to indicate that the sender should stop sending data.
Flow control is released once the incoming buffer has at least MODEM_CMUX_MTU
bytes free again.
This only works if the peer supports MSC messages.
Disable flow control by setting this value to 0.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Modem modules > Modem CMUX module

symbols.name: CONFIG_MODEM_CMUX_MTU

symbols.name: CONFIG_MODEM_CMUX_T2_TIMEOUT
symbols.help:
Response Timer for multiplexer control channel (T2).
Time in milliseconds to wait for a response to a multiplexer control
command before considering the link dead.
NOTE: Zephyr's CMUX implementation deviates from the 3GPP TS 27.010
specification by using T1 for all retry timers and T2 only for
a total response timeout.

symbols.name: CONFIG_MODEM_HL78XX_EDRX_IDLE_TIMEOUT
symbols.prompt: eDRX idle timeout in seconds before allowing sleep
symbols.help:
Unlike PSM (which sends +PSMEV URC), eDRX provides no explicit
notification that the modem is ready to sleep. This timeout is used
as an inactivity detector: every AT command resets the timer. When
the timer expires (no AT activity), the WAKE pin is pulled LOW to
allow the modem to enter eDRX low-power sleep.
The value should be longer than the Paging Time Window (PTW) to
avoid pulling WAKE LOW while the modem is still in a paging cycle.
Default: 10 seconds.

symbols.name: CONFIG_MODEM_SOCKET
symbols.help:
This layer provides much of the groundwork for keeping track of
modem "sockets" throughout their lifecycle (from the initial offload
API calls through the command handler call back layers).
To configure this layer for use, create a modem_socket_config
object with your socket data and pass it's reference to
modem_socket_init().
Note that the modem socket uses runtime allocated file descriptors
reserved from the fdtable, for which the max count is set using the
Kconfig option ZVFS_OPEN_MAX. Make sure to update this value as both
the modem sockets and the POSIX_API, if used, share them.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Device Drivers > Modem drivers

symbols.name: CONFIG_MODEM_SOCKET_PACKET_COUNT
symbols.prompt: Maximum number of stored packet sizes per socket
symbols.help:
As the modem indicates more data is available to be received,
these values are organized into "packets".  This setting limits
the maximum number of packet sizes the socket can keep track of.

symbols.name: CONFIG_MPU_GAP_FILLING
symbols.prompt: Force MPU to be filling in background memory regions
symbols.help:
This Kconfig option instructs the MPU driver to enforce
a full kernel SRAM partitioning, when it programs the
dynamic MPU regions (user thread stack, PRIV stack guard
and application memory domains) during context-switch. We
allow this to be a configurable option, in order to be able
to switch the option off and have an increased number of MPU
regions available for application memory domain programming.

Notes:
An increased number of MPU regions should only be required,
when building with USERSPACE support. As a result, when we
build without USERSPACE support, gap filling should always
be required.

When the option is switched off, access to memory areas not
covered by explicit MPU regions is restricted to privileged
code on an ARCH-specific basis. Refer to ARCH-specific
documentation for more information on how this option is
used.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > MPU features

symbols.name: CONFIG_MPU_STACK_GUARD_MIN_SIZE_FLOAT
symbols.help:
Minimum size (and alignment when applicable) of an ARM MPU
region, which guards the stack of a thread that is using the
Floating Point (FP) context. The width of the guard is set to
128, to accommodate the length of a Cortex-M exception stack
frame when the floating point context is active. The FP context
is only stacked in sharing FP registers mode, therefore, the
option is applicable only when FPU_SHARING is selected.

symbols.name: CONFIG_MQTT_CLEAN_SESSION
symbols.help:
When a client connects to a MQTT broker using a persistent session,
the message broker saves all subscriptions. When the client
disconnects, the message broker stores unacknowledged QoS 1 messages
and new QoS 1 messages published to topics to which the client is
subscribed. When the client reconnects to the persistent session,
all subscriptions are reinstated and all stored messages are sent to
the client. Setting this flag to 0 allows the client to create a
persistent session.

symbols.help:

needs to know how long your addresses are. Set this to the maximum
length in bytes of the address data structure for your implemented transport.

symbols.name: CONFIG_MULTIBOOT
symbols.help:
Embed a multiboot header in the output executable. This is used
by some boot loaders (e.g., GRUB) when loading Zephyr. It is safe
to leave this option on if you're not sure. It only expands the
text segment by 12-16 bytes and is typically ignored if not needed.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > X86 Architecture Options

symbols.name: CONFIG_MULTIBOOT_INFO
symbols.help:
Multiboot passes a pointer to an information structure to the
kernel entry point. Some drivers (e.g., the multiboot framebuffer
display driver) need to refer to information in this structure,
and so set this option to preserve the data in a permanent location.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > X86 Architecture Options > Generate multiboot header

symbols.help: Use the multiboot memory map if the loader provides one.

symbols.name: CONFIG_MULTITHREADING
symbols.help:
If disabled, only the main thread is available, so a main() function
must be provided. Interrupts are available. Kernel objects will most
probably not behave as expected, especially with regards to pending,
since the main thread cannot pend, it being the only thread in the
system.

Many drivers and subsystems will not work with this option
set to 'n'; disable only when you REALLY know what you are
doing.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > General Kernel Options

symbols.name: CONFIG_MULTI_HEAP
symbols.help:
Allows multiple sys_heap regions to be unified under a single
allocation API.  Sometimes apps need the ability to share multiple
discontiguous regions in a single "heap", or
to have memory of different "types" be allocated heuristically based
on usage (e.g. cacheability, latency, power...).  This allows a
user-specified function to select the underlying memory to use for
each application.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Additional libraries > Heap and Memory Allocation

symbols.name: CONFIG_MULTI_LEVEL_INTERRUPTS
symbols.help:
Multiple levels of interrupts are normally used to increase the
number of addressable interrupts in a system. For example, if two
levels are used, a second level interrupt aggregator would combine
all interrupts routed to it into one IRQ line in the first level
interrupt controller. If three levels are used, a third level
aggregator combines its input interrupts into one IRQ line at the
second level. The number of interrupt levels is usually determined
by the hardware. (The term "aggregator" here means "interrupt
controller".)
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Device Drivers > Interrupt controller drivers

symbols.help:

symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > Link layer options > Ethernet support

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_ARP_GRATUITOUS
symbols.help:
Gratuitous in this case means a ARP request or reply that is not
normally needed according to the ARP specification but could be used
in some cases. A gratuitous ARP request is a ARP request packet where
the source and destination IP are both set to the IP of the machine
issuing the packet and the destination MAC is the broadcast address
ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff. Ordinarily, no reply packet will occur.
A gratuitous ARP reply is a reply to which no request has been made.

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_CONTEXT_NET_PKT_POOL
symbols.help:
If enabled, then it is possible to fine-tune network packet pool
for each context when sending network data. If this setting is
enabled, then you should define the context pools in your application
using NET_PKT_TX_POOL_DEFINE() and NET_PKT_DATA_POOL_DEFINE()
macros and tie these pools to desired context using the
net_context_setup_pools() function.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_CONTEXT_PRIORITY
symbols.help:
It is possible to prioritize network traffic. This requires
also traffic class support to work as expected.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_CONTEXT_RCVBUF
symbols.help:
If is possible to define the maximum socket receive buffer per socket.
The default value is set by CONFIG_NET_TCP_MAX_RECV_WINDOW_SIZE. For
TCP sockets, the rcvbuf will determine the receive window size.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_CONTEXT_RCVTIMEO
symbols.help:
It is possible to time out receiving a network packet. The timeout
time is configurable run-time in the application code. For network
sockets timeout is configured per socket with
setsockopt(sock, SOL_SOCKET, SO_RCVTIMEO, ...) function.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_CONTEXT_RECV_HOPLIMIT
symbols.prompt: Add receive hop limit (IPv6) or TTL (IPv4) support to net_context
symbols.help:
Allow to set the IPV6_RECVHOPLIMIT or IP_RECVTTL flags on a socket.
This way user can get extra information about hop limit (IPv6) or TTL (IPv4) in the
socket.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_CONTEXT_RECV_PKTINFO
symbols.prompt: Add receive PKTINFO support to net_context
symbols.help:
Allow to set the IP_PKTINFO or IPV6_RECVPKTINFO flags on a socket.
This way user can get extra information about the received data in the
socket.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_CONTEXT_REUSEADDR
symbols.help:
Allow to set the SO_REUSEADDR flag on a socket. This enables multiple
sockets to bind to the same local IP address.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_CONTEXT_REUSEPORT
symbols.help:
Allow to set the SO_REUSEPORT flag on a socket. This enables multiple
sockets to bind to the same local IP address and port combination.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_CONTEXT_SNDBUF
symbols.help:
It is possible to define the maximum socket send buffer per socket.
For TCP sockets, the sndbuf will determine the total size of queued
data in the TCP layer.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_CONTEXT_SNDTIMEO
symbols.help:
It is possible to time out sending a network packet. The timeout
time is configurable run-time in the application code. For network
sockets timeout is configured per socket with
setsockopt(sock, SOL_SOCKET, SO_SNDTIMEO, ...) function.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_CONTEXT_SYNC_RECV
symbols.prompt: Support synchronous functionality in net_context_recv() API
symbols.help:
You can disable sync support to save some memory if you are calling
net_context_recv() in async way only when timeout is set to 0.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_CONTEXT_TIMESTAMPING
symbols.help:
Allow to set the TIMESTAMPING option on a socket. This way timestamp for a network
packet will be added to the net_pkt structure.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_CONTEXT_TXTIME
symbols.help:

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_DEBUG_NET_PKT_NON_FRAGILE_ACCESS
symbols.prompt: Reduce r/w fragility by resetting the packet cursor when freed
symbols.help:
This MUST not be used unless you have an hard to catch bug. This will
reset the pkt cursor when it's freed, so any subsequent r/w operations
will not segfault, but just bail out and hopefully it will enable you
to know who/where the packet was freed already. Do not set this, by
any means, unless you are actively debugging.

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_DHCPV4_ACCEPT_UNICAST

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_DHCPV4_DNS_SERVER_VIA_INTERFACE
symbols.prompt: Make DNS servers specific to the network interface
symbols.help:
If this is set, then if the system has multiple network interfaces
and each has DHCP enabled, then assign DNS servers received from that
network interface, to that specific interface.
If this option is not set, then any interface can be used for all
the configured DNS server addresses when doing DNS queries.
Example: We receive DNS server 192.0.2.53 DHCPv4 option from Wi-Fi
interface and DNS server 198.51.100.53 from Ethernet interface.
When this option is set, the DNS resolver will use DNS server
192.0.2.53 when sending DNS query to the Wi-Fi interface and DNS
server 198.51.100.53 when sending DNS query to the Ethernet
interface.

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_DHCPV4_SERVER_ADDR_DECLINE_TIME
symbols.prompt: The time IPv4 addresses remains blocked after conflict detection (seconds)
symbols.help:
In case IPv4 address becomes blocked (either because of receiving
Decline message or due to ICMP probe detecting conflict), the address
can no longer be assigned. This timeout specifies how long the address
remains in the Declined state.
Note, that the server may try to reuse the oldest declined address in
case it runs out of free addresses to assign.

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_DHCPV4_SERVER_NAK_UNRECOGNIZED_REQUESTS
symbols.prompt: Reply with NAK for DHCP Requests from clients we do not recognize
symbols.help:
Zephyr's DHCPv4 server does not implement persistent storage of address
leases. As a result, all leases are lost on reboot, which can cause
delays with clients starting in INIT-REBOOT state and thus sending
(potentially several) Requests before attempting full Discover-Request
procedure. Enabling this config will violate the RFC in this regard, as
instead of staying silent for unrecognized Request messages, the server
will send a NAK, informing the client it should proceed with a full
procedure.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > Network additional services > DHCPv4 server

server should provide to clients when they request an IP address. The
DHCPv4 server adds this DNS server address in the DHCP offer and
acknowledgment messages sent to the clients, allowing them to use the
specified DNS server for name resolution.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > Network additional services > DHCPv4 server

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_IPV4_MAPPING_TO_IPV6
symbols.prompt: Support IPv4 mapped on IPv6 addresses
symbols.help:
Support v4-mapped-on-v6 address type. This allows IPv4 and IPv6
to share a local port space. When the application gets an IPv4
connection or packet to an IPv6 socket, its source address will
be mapped to IPv6. This is turned off by default which means
that IPV6_V6ONLY socket option is always on. If you enable this
option, then you can still control the behaviour of the socket
via the IPV6_V6ONLY option at runtime.

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_IPV6_FRAGMENT
symbols.help:
IPv6 fragmentation is disabled by default. This saves memory and
should not cause issues normally as we support anyway the minimum
length IPv6 packets (1280 bytes). If you enable fragmentation
support, please increase amount of RX data buffers so that larger
than 1280 byte packets can be received.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack > IPv6

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_IPV6_FRAGMENT_MAX_COUNT
symbols.prompt: How many packets to reassemble at a time
symbols.help:
How many fragmented IPv6 packets can be waiting reassembly
simultaneously. Each fragment count might use up to 1280 bytes
of memory so you need to plan this and increase the network buffer
count.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack > IPv6 > Support IPv6 fragmentation

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_IPV6_FRAGMENT_MAX_PKT
symbols.prompt: How many fragments can be handled to reassemble a packet
symbols.help:
Incoming fragments are stored in per-packet queue before being
reassembled. This value defines the number of fragments that
can be handled at the same time to reassemble a single packet.

We do not have to accept IPv6 packets larger than 1500 bytes
(RFC 2460 ch 5). This means that we should receive everything
within the first two fragments. The first one being 1280 bytes and
the second one 220 bytes.

You can increase this value if you expect packets with more
than two fragments.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack > IPv6 > Support IPv6 fragmentation

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_IPV6_FRAGMENT_TIMEOUT
symbols.prompt: How long to wait the fragments to receive
symbols.help:
How long to wait for IPv6 fragment to arrive before the reassembly
will timeout. RFC 2460 chapter 4.5 tells to wait for 60 seconds but
this might be too long in memory constrained devices. This value
is in seconds.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack > IPv6 > Support IPv6 fragmentation

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_IPV6_IID_EUI_64
symbols.help:
Generate IID from modified EUI-64 a.k.a MAC address. This is the
legacy way described in RFC 4291 chapter 2.5.1
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack > IPv6 > IPv6 Interface Identifier (IID) generation

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_IPV6_IID_GENERATION
symbols.help:
Determines how the IPv6 Interface Identifier (IID) is generated.
By default the legacy format using EUI-64 (MAC address) specified in
RFC 4291 chapter 2.5.1 is used.
User can also choose to use stable IID specified in RFC 7217 in which
case a randomized IID is generated for each network interface.
The stable IID enhances privacy by having a different IID for each
network interface.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack > IPv6

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_IPV6_IID_STABLE
symbols.help:
Generate a stable IID described in RFC 7217. This option specifies a
method for generating IPv6 Interface Identifiers to be used with
IPv6 Stateless Address Autoconfiguration (SLAAC), such that an IPv6
address configured using this method is stable within each subnet,
but the corresponding Interface Identifier changes when the host
moves from one network to another. This method is meant to be an
alternative to generating Interface Identifiers based on hardware
addresses (e.g., IEEE LAN Media Access Control (MAC) addresses),
such that the benefits of stable addresses can be achieved without
sacrificing the security and privacy of users.
Currently the stable IID generation is disabled for 6lo networks
because of header compression.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack > IPv6 > IPv6 Interface Identifier (IID) generation

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_IPV6_PE
symbols.help:
This enables IPv6 privacy extension (RFC 8981) support.
The interface identifier is randomized and SLAAC addresses
generated from it will expire. This requires that applications are
prepared to use new IPv6 addresses when old ones will expire.
Note that you should make sure that the value of config option
CONFIG_NET_IF_UNICAST_IPV6_ADDR_COUNT should be large enough so that
two PE generated IPv6 addresses can be added to the network interface

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_L2_IEEE802154_RADIO_ALOHA
symbols.prompt: IEEE 802.15.4 Aloha medium access protocol (CCA mode 4)
symbols.help:
Use Aloha mechanism (send without any clear channel assessment) to
transmit packets. This is a simplistic way of transmitting packets
and fits low duty-cycle contexts where the radio spectrum is not
too heavily loaded (see IEEE 802.15.4-2020, section 10.2.8). The
current implementation does not randomize channel access.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > Link layer options > IEEE 802.15.4 Radio > IEEE 802.15.4 Radio > Radio channel access protocol

symbols.help:

to transmit packets. This is the most common way of mediating radio
channel access and fits most usage scenarios (see IEEE 802.15.4-2020,
sections 6.2.5.1 and 10.2.8).
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > Link layer options > IEEE 802.15.4 Radio > IEEE 802.15.4 Radio > Radio channel access protocol

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_L2_PPP_THREAD_PRIO
symbols.prompt: Priority of the PPP TX thread
symbols.help:
Set the priority of the PPP TX thread, that handles all
transmission of PPP packets.
Value 0 = highest priortity.
When CONFIG_NET_TC_THREAD_COOPERATIVE = y, lowest priority is
CONFIG_NUM_COOP_PRIORITIES-1 else lowest priority is
CONFIG_NUM_PREEMPT_PRIORITIES-1.
When using PPP in combination with TCP, make sure the priority
is higher (or equal) than the TCP work queue, otherwise the
TCP stack will consume all net_bufs before transferring
execution to the lower layer network stack, with a high risk of
running out of net_bufs.

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_MGMT_EVENT
symbols.prompt: Add support for runtime network event notifications
symbols.help:
This adds support for the stack to notify events towards any
relevant listener. This can be necessary when application
(or else) needs to be notified on a specific network event
(ip address change for instance) to trigger some related work.

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_MGMT_EVENT_DIRECT

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_MGMT_EVENT_INFO

symbols.help:

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_NAMESPACE_COMPAT_MODE
symbols.help:
The networking APIs and code is now namespaced i.e., relevant network
APIs now have either net_, NET_ or ZSOCK_ prefixes. This avoids
circular dependency against a Posix subsystem which might define
duplicate symbols. The compatibility mode will be deprecated in the
future and eventually removed.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_NATIVE
symbols.help:
Enables Zephyr native IP stack. If you disable this, then
you need to enable the offloading support if you want to
have IP connectivity.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_NATIVE_OFFLOADED_SOCKETS
symbols.help:
Offloaded sockets for Native Simulator utilize host BSD sockets API (like socket(),
connect(), send(), recvfrom(), etc.) in order to provide networking capability.

This driver main advantage is that it is possible to use this driver without any
additional setup on the host side, unlike with the native TAP Ethernet driver.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Device Drivers > Network drivers

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_NATIVE_OFFLOADED_SOCKETS_CONNECTIVITY_SIM
symbols.prompt: Support for the network connectivity API
symbols.help:
Simulate an interface that transitions through the dormant state based on calls
to the network connectivity API, after some delay.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Device Drivers > Network drivers > Native Simulator offloaded sockets

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_NATIVE_OFFLOADED_SOCKETS_CONNECTIVITY_SIM_AUTO_CONNECT
symbols.help:
If this option is set the Connection Manager will automatically call connect after the
network interface has been brought up. This option sets the default value, the option has
a corresponding flag that can be set at run time by calling conn_mgr_if_set_flag().
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Device Drivers > Network drivers > Native Simulator offloaded sockets > Support for the network connectivity API

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_NATIVE_OFFLOADED_SOCKETS_EPOLL_WAIT_INTERVAL
symbols.prompt: Interval between epoll_wait() calls (in simulated microseconds)
symbols.help:
Number of simulated microseconds before next epoll_wait() call, when there were no pending
events detected.

Decrease that value when lower network traffic latency is expected, at the expense of more
CPU processing overhead.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Device Drivers > Network drivers > Native Simulator offloaded sockets

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_PKT_TIMESTAMP
symbols.help:
Enable network packet timestamp support. This is needed for
example in gPTP which needs to know how long it takes to send
a network packet or for timed radio protocols like IEEE 802.15.4

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_PKT_TIMESTAMP_THREAD
symbols.help:
Create a TX timestamp thread that will pass the timestamped network
packets to some other module like gPTP for further processing.
If you just want to timestamp network packets and get information
how long the network packets flow in the system, you can disable
the thread support.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack > Network packet timestamp support

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_PKT_TXTIME
symbols.help:
Enable network packet TX time support. This is needed for
when the application wants to set the exact time when the network
packet should be sent.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_PKT_TXTIME_STATS
symbols.help:
Enable network packet TX time statistics support. This is used to
calculate how long on average it takes for a packet to travel from
application to just before it is sent to network. The TX timing
information can then be seen in network interface statistics in
net-shell.
The RX calculation is done only for UDP, TCP or RAW packets,
but for TX we do not know the protocol so the TX packet timing is
done for all network protocol packets.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_DNS_BACKOFF_INTERVAL
symbols.prompt: Backoff interval for the DNS timeout
symbols.help:
This variable is related to the DNS timeout. If the DNS timeout is
smaller than this value, then this value is ignored. If the timeout
is larger, then this variable specifies time in milliseconds after
which DNS query is re-tried. If there is no reply, the backoff
interval is doubled and query is retried.
Example:
   The CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_DNS_TIMEOUT is set to 17000 (17 secs).
   This value is 5000 (5 sec). If there is no reply from DNS server
   within 5 secs, a 2nd query is done with timeout set to 10 sec (5 * 2).
   If no reply is received, a 3rd query is done after 15 sec (5 + 5 * 2),
   and the timeout is set to 2 sec so that the total timeout is 17 seconds.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > Network Libraries > BSD Sockets compatible API

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_DNS_TIMEOUT
symbols.prompt: Timeout value in milliseconds for DNS queries
symbols.help:
This variable specifies time in milliseconds after which DNS
query is considered timeout. Minimum timeout is 1 second and
maximum timeout is 5 min. If the value is higher than
CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_DNS_BACKOFF_INTERVAL, then we try multiple
times with exponential backoff until the timeout is reached.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > Network Libraries > BSD Sockets compatible API

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_DTLS_MAX_FRAGMENT_LENGTH
symbols.prompt: Maximum DTLS fragment size in bytes
symbols.help:
This variable specifies the Maximum Fragment Length (MFL) value to
be used with DTLS connection when MBEDTLS_SSL_OUT_CONTENT_LEN and
MBEDTLS_SSL_IN_CONTENT_LEN are set to larger values (for TLS).

With DTLS the MFL should be kept under the network MTU, to avoid
IP fragmentation.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > Network Libraries > BSD Sockets compatible API > DTLS socket support

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_DTLS_SENDMSG_BUF_SIZE
symbols.prompt: Intermediate buffer size for DTLS sendmsg()
symbols.help:
Size of the intermediate buffer for DTLS sendmsg() function. The
intermediate buffer is needed, as sendmsg() for DGRAM is expected to
send all of the data in a single datagram, therefore all data provided
in msghdr structure need to be linearized before passing to mbed TLS.
The buffer size can be set to 0, in that case data linearizing for
DTLS sockets is disabled. In result, sendmsg() will only accept msghdr
with a single non-empty iov buffer.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > Network Libraries > BSD Sockets compatible API > DTLS socket support

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_DTLS_TIMEOUT
symbols.prompt: Timeout value in milliseconds for DTLS connection
symbols.help:
This variable specifies time in milliseconds after which DTLS
connection is considered dead by TLS server and DTLS resources are
freed. This is needed to prevent situation when DTLS client shuts down
without closing connection gracefully, which can prevent other peers
from connecting. Value of 0 indicates no timeout - resources will be
freed only when connection is gracefully closed by peer sending TLS
notification or socket is closed.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > Network Libraries > BSD Sockets compatible API > DTLS socket support

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_OFFLOAD
symbols.help:
Enables direct offloading of socket operations to dedicated TCP/IP
hardware.
This feature is intended to save resources by bypassing the Zephyr
TCP/IP stack in the case where there is only one network interface
required in the system, providing full BSD socket offload capability.
As a result, it bypasses any potential IP routing that Zephyr might
provide between multiple network interfaces.
See NET_OFFLOAD for a more deeply integrated approach which offloads
from the net_context() API within the Zephyr IP stack.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > Network Libraries > BSD Sockets compatible API

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_OFFLOAD_DISPATCHER
symbols.help:
If enabled, an intermediate socket offloading layer is included
(called socket dispatcher), allowing to select an offloaded network
interface and thus socket implementation with SO_BINDTODEVICE socket
option. This can be useful, when multiple offloaded sockets
implementations are available in the system, allowing to easily bind
a socket to a particular implementation.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > Network Libraries > BSD Sockets compatible API

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_OFFLOAD_DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_MAX
symbols.prompt: Maximum number of dispatcher sockets created
symbols.help:
Maximum number of dispatcher sockets created at a time. Note, that
only sockets that has not been dispatched yet count into the limit.
After a proper socket has been created for a given file descriptor,
the dispatcher context is released and can be reused.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > Network Libraries > BSD Sockets compatible API > Intermediate socket offloading layer

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_OFFLOAD_PRIORITY
symbols.prompt: Default processing priority for offloaded sockets
symbols.help:
Processing priority for offloaded sockets.

If native TLS is enabled, lower value than NET_SOCKETS_TLS_PRIORITY
means that TLS will be offloaded as well (if supported by offloaded
socket implementation). Higher value than NET_SOCKETS_TLS_PRIORITY
means that native TLS will be used.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > Network Libraries > BSD Sockets compatible API

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_PACKET
symbols.help:
This is an initial version of packet socket support (special type
raw socket). Packets are passed to and from the device driver
without any changes in the packet headers. It's API caller
responsibility to provide all the headers (e.g L2, L3 and so on)
while sending. While receiving, packets (including all the headers)
will be fed to sockets unchanged as provided by the driver.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > Network Libraries > BSD Sockets compatible API

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_PACKET_DGRAM
symbols.help:
For AF_PACKET sockets with SOCK_DGRAM type, the L2 header
is removed before the packet is passed to the user.  Packets sent
through a SOCK_DGRAM packet socket get a suitable L2 header based
on the information in the net_sockaddr_ll destination address before
they are queued.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > Network Libraries > BSD Sockets compatible API > Packet socket support

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_PRIORITY_DEFAULT

Default processing priority for socket implementations. This defines

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_SERVICE

The socket service can monitor multiple sockets and save memory

Note that you need to set CONFIG_ZVFS_POLL_MAX high enough
so that enough sockets entries can be serviced. This depends on

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_SERVICE_THREAD_PRIO
symbols.prompt: Priority of the socket service dispatcher thread

Note that >= 0 value means preemptive thread priority, the lowest

Highest preemptive thread priority is 0.
Lowest cooperative thread priority is -1.
Highest cooperative thread priority is -NUM_COOP_PRIORITIES.

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS_TLS_SET_MAX_FRAGMENT_LENGTH
symbols.help:
Call mbedtls_ssl_conf_max_frag_len() on created TLS context
configuration, so that Maximum Fragment Length (MFL) will be sent to
peer using RFC 6066 max_fragment_length extension.

Maximum Fragment Length (MFL) value is automatically chosen based on
MBEDTLS_SSL_OUT_CONTENT_LEN and MBEDTLS_SSL_IN_CONTENT_LEN mbed TLS
macros (which are configured by CONFIG_MBEDTLS_SSL_MAX_CONTENT_LEN in
case of default mbed TLS config). With DTLS, MFL value may be further
limited with NET_SOCKETS_DTLS_MAX_FRAGMENT_LENGTH.

This is mostly useful for TLS client side to tell TLS server what is
the maximum supported receive record length.

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_TCP_MAX_RECV_WINDOW_SIZE
symbols.prompt: Maximum receive window size to use
symbols.help:
This value defines the maximum TCP receive window size. Increasing
this value can improve connection throughput, but requires more

The default value 0 lets the TCP stack select the value
according to amount of network buffers configured in the system.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack > TCP

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_TCP_MAX_SEND_WINDOW_SIZE
symbols.prompt: Maximum sending window size to use
symbols.help:

according to amount of network buffers configured in the system.

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_TCP_PKT_ALLOC_TIMEOUT
symbols.prompt: How long to wait for a TCP packet allocation (in ms)
symbols.help:
The TCP network stack allocates packets from the buffers and the
allocation can take some time depending on the situation.
This value indicates how long the stack should wait for the packet to
be allocated, before returning an internal error and trying again.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack > TCP

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_TCP_PRESERVE_CONTEXT_STATE_ON_IFACE_DOWN
symbols.prompt: Keep the TCP connection contexts open when interface goes down
symbols.help:
Zephyr by default closes all TCP contexts associated with a given
network interface when the interface goes down. This leads to
reporting an error on the associated network socket, allowing the
application to reopen sockets (for example in case of a network or
an IP address change).
It's been reported however that in certain cases this behavior is
undesirable. If this option is enabled, the TCP stack won't
close any TCP contexts when the network interface is going down.
Therefore, it is the application's responsibility to monitor the IP
address or network interface state changes, and restart the TCP
sockets when needed. Enable this option only if you can guarantee that
the application handles that properly.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack > TCP

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_TCP_RANDOMIZED_RTO
symbols.help:
It can happen that two similar stacks enter a retransmission cycle
due to a packet collision. If the transmission timeout is the same
both stacks will retry at the same moment resulting in another
collision. By introducing a randomized retry timeout, the chance of
a second collision is reduced and it reduces further the more
retransmissions occur.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack > TCP

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_TCP_RECV_QUEUE_TIMEOUT
symbols.prompt: How long to queue received data (in ms)
symbols.help:
If we receive out-of-order TCP data, we queue it. This value tells
how long the data is kept before it is discarded if we have not been
able to pass the data to the application. If set to 0, then receive
queueing is not enabled. The value is in milliseconds.
Note that we only queue data sequentially in current version i.e.,
there should be no holes in the queue. For example, if we receive
SEQs 5,4,3,6 and are waiting SEQ 2, the data in segments 3,4,5,6 is
queued (in this order), and then given to application when we receive
SEQ 2. But if we receive SEQs 5,4,3,7 then the SEQ 7 is discarded
because the list would not be sequential as number 6 is be missing.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack > TCP

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_TCP_REJECT_CONN_WITH_RST
symbols.prompt: Reject connection attempts on unbound TCP ports with RST
symbols.help:
If enabled, TCP stack will reject connection attempts on unbound ports
with TCP RST packet.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack > TCP

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_TCP_RETRY_COUNT
symbols.prompt: Maximum number of TCP segment retransmissions
symbols.help:
The following formula can be used to determine the time (in ms)
that a segment will be be buffered awaiting retransmission:
n=NET_TCP_RETRY_COUNT
Sum((1<<n) * NET_TCP_INIT_RETRANSMISSION_TIMEOUT)
n=0
With the default value of 9, the IP stack will try to
retransmit for up to 1:42 minutes.  This is as close as possible
to the minimum value recommended by RFC1122 (1:40 minutes).
Only 5 bits are dedicated for the retransmission count, so accepted
values are in the 0-31 range.  It's highly recommended to not go
below 9, though.
Should a retransmission timeout occur, the receive callback is
called with -ETIMEDOUT error code and the context is dereferenced.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack > TCP

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_TCP_TIME_WAIT_DELAY
symbols.prompt: How long to wait in TIME_WAIT state (in milliseconds)
symbols.help:
To avoid a (low-probability) issue when delayed packets from
previous connection get delivered to next connection reusing
the same local/remote ports, RFC 793 (TCP) suggests to keep
an old, closed connection in a special "TIME_WAIT" state for
the duration of 2*MSL (Maximum Segment Lifetime). The RFC
suggests to use MSL of 2 minutes, but notes "This is an
engineering choice, and may be changed if experience indicates
it is desirable to do so." For low-resource systems, having
large MSL may lead to quick resource exhaustion (and related
DoS attacks). At the same time, the issue of packet misdelivery
is largely alleviated in the modern TCP stacks by using random,
non-repeating port numbers and initial sequence numbers. Due
to this, Zephyr uses much lower value of 1500ms by default.
Value of 0 disables TIME_WAIT state completely.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack > TCP

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_TCP_WORKER_PRIO
symbols.prompt: Priority of the TCP work queue
symbols.help:
Set the priority of the TCP worker queue, that handles all
transmission and maintenance within the TCP stack.
Value 0 = highest priortity.
When CONFIG_NET_TC_THREAD_COOPERATIVE = y, lowest priority is
CONFIG_NUM_COOP_PRIORITIES-1 else lowest priority is
CONFIG_NUM_PREEMPT_PRIORITIES-1.
Make sure the priority is lower than lower layer TX threads to
avoid the TCP stack consume all net_bufs before transferring
execution to the lower layer network stack, with a high risk of
running out of net_bufs.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack > TCP

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_TC_RX_COUNT
symbols.prompt: How many Rx traffic classes to have for each network device
symbols.help:
Define how many Rx traffic classes (queues) the system should have
when receiving a network packet. The network packet priority can then
be mapped to this traffic class so that higher prioritized packets
can be processed before lower prioritized ones. Each queue is handled
by a separate thread which will need RAM for stack space.
Only increase the value from 1 if you really need this feature.
The default value is 1 which means that all the network traffic is
handled equally. In this implementation, the higher traffic class
value corresponds to lower thread priority.
If you select 0 here, then it means that all the network traffic
is pushed from the driver to application thread without any
intermediate RX queue. There is always a receive socket queue between
device driver and application. Disabling RX thread means that the
network device driver, that is typically running in IRQ context, will
handle the packet all the way to the application. This might cause
other incoming packets to be lost if the RX processing takes long
time.
Note that if USERSPACE support is enabled, then currently we need to
enable at least 1 RX thread.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack

symbols.name: CONFIG_NET_TC_RX_SKIP_FOR_HIGH_PRIO
symbols.prompt: Push high priority packets directly to the application
symbols.help:
If this is set, then high priority (>= NET_PRIORITY_CA) net_pkt will
be pushed directly to the application and will skip the traffic class
queues. If you select this option, then it means that high priority
network traffic is pushed from the driver to the application thread
without any intermediate RX queue. If the network device driver is
running in IRQ context, it will handle the packet all the way to the
application. This might cause other incoming packets to be lost if
the RX processing takes long time.
This is currently not enabled by default.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > Subsystems and OS Services > Networking > Link layer and networking (including IP) > IP stack

symbols.name: CONFIG_NEWLIB_LIBC
symbols.help:

symbols.name: CONFIG_NEWLIB_LIBC_ALIGNED_HEAP_SIZE
symbols.help:
If user mode is enabled, and MPU hardware has requirements that
regions be sized to a power of two and aligned to their size,
and user mode threads need to access this heap, then this is necessary
to properly define an MPU region for the heap.

If this is left at 0, then remaining system RAM will be used for this
area and it may not be possible to program it as an MPU region.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > C Library

symbols.name: CONFIG_NEWLIB_LIBC_CUSTOM_SBRK
symbols.help:

may need to use the remaining RAM for also other purposes than heap.

the image.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > C Library

symbols.name: CONFIG_NEWLIB_LIBC_FLOAT_SCANF

symbols.help:

libc heap usage, such as the heap resize.

symbols.name: CONFIG_NEWLIB_LIBC_MAX_MAPPED_REGION_SIZE
symbols.prompt: Maximum memory mapped for newlib heap
symbols.help:
On MMU-based systems, indicates the maximum amount of memory which
will be used for the newlib malloc() heap. The actual amount of
memory used will be the minimum of this value and the amount of
free physical memory at kernel boot.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > C Library

symbols.name: CONFIG_NEWLIB_LIBC_MIN_REQUIRED_HEAP_SIZE
symbols.help:
Specifies the amount of memory space that must be available for the
newlib heap. An assertion failure message will be displayed during
initialization if the memory space available for the newlib heap is
smaller than this value.
symbols.menupath: (Top) > C Library

The newlib provided by the Zephyr SDK does not include all mandatory POSIX limits.
However, some external newlib-based toolchains do.

Disable this option if your toolchain's newlib already includes all mandatory POSIX
limits.
